articles.headline: Iran Condemns New US Economic Sanctions as State Terrorism
articles.summary: Iran has condemned new US economic sanctions as “state terrorism,” stating that other nations are legally bound to ignore them. The US Treasury announced additional measures targeting Iran-linked entities in Hong Kong and the UAE. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Aragchi appealed to the US to resume negotiations, emphasizing that military and economic pressure will not resolve the conflict.

articles.headline: Search Continues for 2,400 Missing After Glacial Collapse Near Tibet
articles.summary: The number of missing persons in Nepal and China jumped to over 2,400 after a glacial collapse triggered massive debris flows. Rescuers have recovered 584 bodies so far. India’s foreign ministry reported 320 Indians missing in Nepal and 400 stranded in China. The disaster, the deadliest since 2015, was caused by ice and rock falling over a kilometer into the valley below.

articles.headline: Bihar to Replace Fail With Eligible for Skill Training Marksheets
articles.summary: The Bihar government will remove the word “Fail” from Class 10 and 12 marksheets to reduce student stigma. Education Minister Mithilesh Tiwari announced that students who do not clear exams will instead be marked “Eligible for Skill Training.” This allows them to opt for vocational programs under the state open school board. The initiative is aimed at fostering alternate career paths.

articles.headline: Punjab Social Media Influencer Dies After Being Set on Fire
articles.summary: A 28-year-old social media influencer died in Chandigarh nearly two months after she was allegedly abducted, assaulted, and set on fire in Punjab’s Rupnagar district. Police have registered a case of kidnapping and murder against two acquaintances, Shubhi and Pinda. The victim, a divorcee and mother of a seven-year-old, succumbed to severe burn injuries during treatment.

articles.headline: National Conference MP Ruhullah Mehdi Challenges Party Over Article 370
articles.summary: National Conference MP Aga Syed Ruhullah Mehdi has indicated he will resign from Parliament, but demanded answers on the party’s shifted stance regarding Article 370. Mehdi criticized the party leadership for prioritizing statehood over restored constitutional rights. Party president Farooq Abdullah has asked Mehdi to seek a fresh mandate if he opposes the official party line.

articles.headline: Eight-Year-Old Boy Killed by Pitch Roller at Manesar Cricket Academy
articles.summary: An eight-year-old boy died in IMT Manesar after being crushed by a 750kg pitch roller. The incident occurred when children at the academy accidentally switched on the unsupervised machine's miniature circuit breaker. Police have registered a case following the tragedy, which highlights safety lapses at local sports facilities.

articles.headline: Renewed Search for Elusive Fugitive Sukumara Kurup Following New Claims
articles.summary: The 42-year-old mystery of fugitive Sukumara Kurup has resurfaced following claims by a retired police officer that Kurup is living in Brunei. Kurup vanished in 1984 after faking his death by murdering a man who resembled him to claim insurance money. While new photos suggested his whereabouts, authorities later identified the individual in the pictures as a different person from Thrissur.

articles.headline: Accused in Saif Ali Khan Attack Case to Plead Guilty
articles.summary: Mohammad Shariful Islam, a Bangladeshi national, informed a Mumbai sessions court that he wants to plead guilty for attacking actor Saif Ali Khan during a 2025 robbery attempt. The accused, who previously pleaded not guilty, sought leniency, stating he repents his actions. The court has scheduled the next hearing for September 11.

articles.headline: Alliance Air Flight Suffers Tyre Burst During Landing in Bilaspur
articles.summary: An Alliance Air flight from Delhi carrying 41 people suffered a tyre burst while landing at Bilaspur airport on Friday. All 37 passengers and four crew members were safely evacuated from the aircraft. The airline cancelled the onward flight scheduled from Bilaspur as a result of the incident.

articles.headline: Putin to Meet PM Modi at SCO Summit in Bishkek
articles.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin is scheduled to meet Prime Minister Narendra Modi during the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Summit in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan. The meeting, taking place between August 31 and September 1, will focus on reviewing bilateral relationships. Putin is also expected to meet with the leaders of China and Iran during the summit.

articles.headline: Banks Struggle with Low Recovery in Personal Guarantor Insolvency Cases
articles.summary: Data from the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board shows that creditors have recovered only 1% of admitted claims against personal guarantors since 2020. Despite high-profile cases like Subhash Chandra’s ₹6.5 crore repayment plan, legal experts note that personal insolvency often reveals a lack of attachable assets, failing to significantly offset large corporate defaults.

articles.headline: Karnataka Government Orders Strict Food Safety Measures for Hotels
articles.summary: Karnataka Health Minister UT Khader directed the hotel industry to prioritize public health over profits following a series of hygiene violations. In a high-level meeting, the government ordered scientifically designed storage rooms and strict compliance with food safety regulations. Intensive inspections over the past month revealed deficiencies across several star hotels and eateries.

articles.headline: Karnataka to Develop Five New Industrial Cities with Airport Connectivity
articles.summary: Deputy CM DK Shivakumar has directed officials to identify five cities outside Bengaluru for industrial development to decongest the capital. The plan involves offering special incentives to attract manufacturing in semiconductors, aerospace, and defense. Each city must have airport connectivity and essential infrastructure to facilitate a streamlined single-window approval system.

articles.headline: IAS Officer Gyanendra Gangwar Appears Before CID in KPSC Probe
articles.summary: IAS officer Gyanendra Kumar Gangwar appeared before the CID for questioning regarding alleged irregularities in the KPSC veterinary officer recruitment. The move follows Enforcement Directorate searches at his residence and native place. Gangwar, a former KPSC examination controller, is being investigated for procedural lapses and potential financial misconduct in the selection process.

articles.headline: Kumaraswamy Demands Home Minister Priyank Kharge Resignation Over KPSC Row
articles.summary: Union Minister HD Kumaraswamy demanded the resignation of Karnataka Home Minister Priyank Kharge over alleged KPSC recruitment irregularities. Kumaraswamy questioned why appointments were made despite complaints of OMR-sheet manipulation and missing CCTV footage. He alleged the government ignored evidence of fraud in the selection of Assistant Executive Engineers.

articles.headline: Bengaluru Police Inspector Dies in Madhya Pradesh Bus Accident
articles.summary: Ravi KB, a police inspector from Bengaluru's CEN station, died in a bus accident in Rajgarh, Madhya Pradesh. He was in the state to investigate a cybercrime case when the bus fell into a gorge near Biaora. While his colleagues survived with injuries, Ravi succumbed to his wounds. Karnataka CM DK Shivakumar expressed grief over the dedicated officer's demise.

articles.headline: Police Shoot Suspected Illegal Arms Manufacturer During Bengaluru Encounter
articles.summary: Bengaluru police shot a 34-year-old suspected illegal arms manufacturer, Zeeshan, in the leg during a confrontation in Electronic City. Zeeshan allegedly attacked a police constable with a weapon after being cornered. Police fired a warning shot before shooting him in self-defense. The suspect and an injured constable are currently receiving medical treatment.

articles.headline: Karnataka Opposes Centre Notification on Kasturirangan Report Implementation
articles.summary: Karnataka Deputy CM G Parameshwara condemned the Union government's notification to declare 1,449 villages in the Western Ghats as ecologically sensitive areas. He stated the government would not allow the implementation of the Kasturirangan report, citing concerns over the displacement of lakhs of families. A special legislative session is planned to discuss solutions and protect local interests.

articles.headline: Madras HC Issues Notice to Stalin in Defamation Suit
articles.summary: The Madras High Court issued notices to TN CM MK Stalin and the DMK’s IT wing following a ₹1-crore defamation suit filed by Minister Aadhav Arjuna. Arjuna alleges he was falsely linked to a narcotics case in an X post. He has sought a permanent injunction and an unconditional apology from the party leadership for tarnishing his image.

articles.headline: Eight Keralites and Australian Citizens Still Missing in Nepal Floods
articles.summary: Kerala CM VD Satheesan confirmed that eight people, including four Australian citizens of Kerala origin, remain untraced following flash floods in Nepal. Details have been forwarded to the Ministry of External Affairs for urgent rescue operations. Separately, 19 members of a 23-member Kailash Mansarovar Yatra group from the state have been confirmed safe.

articles.headline: Tamil Nadu CM Vijay Inspects Puzhal Prison and Police Station
articles.summary: Tamil Nadu CM C Joseph Vijay inspected the Puzhal Central Prison and the M3 Puzhal Police Station. He visited inmate workshops, reviewed prison-made products, and assessed the quality of food served to prisoners. The visit included inspections of the library, de-addiction center, and isolation ward to review general administrative standards.

articles.headline: IIT Madras Unveils Phiball a New Three Team Competitive Sport
articles.summary: IIT Madras has introduced ‘Phiball,’ an innovative invasion sport featuring three teams competing simultaneously on a circular court. Unlike traditional two-team sports, Phiball requires players to attack two opponent baskets while defending their own. The sport is designed to test rapid strategic adaptation and was unveiled ahead of National Sports Day.

articles.headline: Singareni Collieries Moves to Explore Gold and Copper in Karnataka
articles.summary: Telangana's Singareni Collieries Company Limited (SCCL) has launched mineral exploration at the Devadurga block in Karnataka. Deputy CM Mallu Bhatti Vikramarka directed officials to use advanced technology to assess gold and copper deposits. The state-owned miner aims to form a joint venture with Hutti Gold Mines to boost domestic production of refined gold.

articles.headline: Dalit Activist Apologises for Alleged Derogatory Remarks Against Sabarimala Deity
articles.summary: Dalit activist Sunny M Kapikkad issued an apology for alleged derogatory comments against Lord Ayyappa following a police case. The remarks, made during a recent event, triggered complaints from the BJP and Sabarimala groups. Kapikkad stated his intention was not to hurt religious sentiments after facing significant backlash and legal pressure.

articles.headline: YSRCP Criticizes AP Government for Inaction Over Rayalaseema Drought
articles.summary: YSR Congress Party leaders alleged that the Andhra Pradesh coalition government has failed to address a severe drought in the Rayalaseema region. Former ministers claimed that kharif cultivation has plummeted to 40% and groundwater levels have dropped by up to 20 meters. They demanded immediate support for farmers facing a lack of irrigation and fodder.

articles.headline: Nepal Flood Debris Chokes Gandak River in UP and Bihar
articles.summary: Heavy silt and debris from Nepal floods have entered the Gandak river system, forcing authorities in Kushinagar and Maharajganj to shut canals. Officials reported nearly 13 cubic metres of added silt, threatening to choke the irrigation network. Items like LPG cylinders and tyres have been spotted in the river, prompting high alerts in downstream villages.

articles.headline: Explosion Reported Near Manipur Government Spokesperson's Residence
articles.summary: An explosion occurred near the residence of Manipur government spokesperson Sapam Ranjan Singh in Imphal West. The blast caused minor damage to compound walls but resulted in no casualties. CM Yumnam Khemchand Singh condemned the act as an attack on democracy, while police registered a case to identify the nature of the explosives used.

articles.headline: Centre Appoints New Senior Officers to National Testing Agency
articles.summary: The Centre has appointed Anshuman Sharma (IRS) as Joint Secretary and Sathiya S (IRS) as Director at the National Testing Agency (NTA). The appointments follow a series of examination-related lapses earlier this year. These moves are part of an ongoing overhaul to strengthen the testing body’s institutional integrity and technical capabilities.

articles.headline: UGC NET Results Announced for Eighty Four Subjects
articles.summary: The National Testing Agency (NTA) announced results for the UGC-NET in 84 subjects, with over 6.07 lakh candidates appearing. More than 4,000 candidates qualified for the Junior Research Fellowship (JRF), while over 97,000 qualified for PhD admissions. Fresh exams were held in some subjects after earlier factual and translation errors were discovered in June.

articles.headline: Defence Ministry Streamlines Export Rules to Target Fifty Thousand Crore Exports
articles.summary: The Ministry of Defence announced reforms to simplify the Open General Export Licence (OGEL) framework, aiming to reach ₹50,000 crore in exports by 2029-30. The new rules enable exporters to self-generate authorizations for multiple consignments of non-lethal items. These changes are expected to benefit MSMEs by allowing faster access to international markets.

articles.headline: Gujarat Police Arrest Three After VHP Protest Over Book Reading
articles.summary: Police in Ahmedabad arrested three people after right-wing groups disrupted a book-reading session featuring works by Malala Yousafzai and Anne Frank. Protesters from the VHP and Bajrang Dal allegedly assaulted participants at AUDA Garden, claiming the books promoted a “pro-Pakistan” mentality. A case has been registered against at least 20 unidentified people for rioting.

articles.headline: White House Reviews Rule to End H1-B Visa Grace Period
articles.summary: The US White House has completed a review of a proposal to eliminate the 60-day grace period for foreign workers following job loss. If finalized, workers on H-1B, L-1, and other visas would be required to leave the US immediately upon termination of employment. The rule change could significantly impact thousands of Indian nationals currently working in the US tech sector.

articles.headline: China Removes Two High Ranking Officers From Central Military Commission
articles.summary: China has removed two senior officers, Zhang Youxia and Liu Zhenli, from its Central Military Commission. State media reported that the officers are being investigated for “serious violations of the law.” The move follows a broader purge within the Chinese military leadership over the past year focused on corruption and loyalty.

articles.headline: US Court Rules Trump Administration Ban on Anthropic Illegal
articles.summary: A US federal judge has ruled that sanctions imposed by the Trump administration against AI firm Anthropic were unlawful. The court found that the government unfairly punished the company during a dispute over the military use of its artificial intelligence technology. The ruling marks a significant legal victory for the AI developer against executive overreach.

articles.headline: Norway King Harald Dies at 89; Succeeded by Haakon VIII
articles.summary: King Harald of Norway passed away at age 89 after a 35-year reign, leading to a period of national mourning. His 53-year-old son succeeded him immediately, taking the name King Haakon VIII. Harald was Europe's oldest reigning monarch and was widely respected for his warmth and for modernizing the Norwegian monarchy through decades of social change.

articles.headline: PM Modi Lauds Jan Dhan Scheme as Accounts Reach 590 Million
articles.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi praised the Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana for achieving 590 million bank accounts with deposits totaling ₹3.16 lakh crore. Celebrating the scheme's 12th anniversary, he noted that 56% of holders are women and 78% are in rural areas. The scheme is credited with rapid financial inclusion and promoting digital transactions among the unbanked.

articles.headline: India Industrial Production Grows Six Point Seven Percent in July
articles.summary: India’s industrial output recorded a 6.7% growth in July, moderating from a 27-month high of 8.8% in June. Manufacturing expanded by 7.3%, driven by motor vehicles and electrical equipment. While mining saw a slight contraction, the electricity sector grew by 8.7%. Experts cited an uncertain external environment and monsoon challenges as factors for the slight slowdown.

articles.headline: Novak Djokovic Explores Career and Defiance in New Documentary
articles.summary: A new documentary, 'The Wolf in Winter', explores Novak Djokovic's career as he prepares for the US Open at age 39. Despite winning nearly every major tennis title, Djokovic remains driven by a stubborn streak and a need to prove critics wrong. The film captures his capacity for pain and the Serbian concept of 'Inat,' or defiance, that fuels his continued participation in professional tennis.

articles.headline: Ryu Jun-yeol Stars in Identity Theft Series Mousetrap on Netflix
articles.summary: In the new Korean series 'Mousetrap', a novelist played by Ryu Jun-yeol discovers his identity and money have been stolen by a mysterious figure. He forms an unlikely partnership with a former loan shark to reclaim his life. The series is currently streaming on Netflix.

articles.headline: Nimisha Sajayan Plays Bhopal Cop in Amazon Prime Film
articles.summary: The film 'Babita Singh Reporting', directed by Ambiecka Pandit, stars Nimisha Sajayan as a cop in Bhopal. The narrative follows her pursuit of a potential murder case while navigating the complex personal demands of her in-laws. The title is available on Amazon Prime.

articles.headline: Mumbai Light Festival Transforms Afghan Church with Projection Mapping
articles.summary: The Mumbai Light Festival is featuring an immersive projection mapping project titled 'Ascension' inside the Grade 1 heritage Afghan Church in Colaba. Created by Floating Canvas Company, the display uses light and celestial imagery to transform the Gothic structure into a canvas of color through August 29.

articles.headline: Rosebush Pruning Black Comedy Starring Callum Turner and Riley Keough
articles.summary: Streaming on MUBI, 'Rosebush Pruning' is a black comedy directed by Karim Aïnouz. Based on the 1965 Italian film 'Fists in the Pocket', the film features an ensemble cast including Callum Turner, Riley Keough, Elle Fanning, and Pamela Anderson exploring the dynamics of a twisted, wealthy family.

articles.headline: Bobby Deol Stars in Harsh Prison Drama Bandar on Zee5
articles.summary: Directed by Anurag Kashyap and written by Sudip Sharma, 'Bandar' stars Bobby Deol as a washed-up TV star facing rape charges. The film focuses on the dangerous conditions of Indian jails and the experiences of undertrials. The cast includes Saba Azad, Sapna Pabbi, and Raj B. Shetty.

articles.headline: Exhibition Grip Hold Pin Explores Indian Wrestling Art in Bengaluru
articles.summary: The Museum of Art & Photography in Bengaluru is hosting 'Grip, Hold, Pin', an exhibition examining the sport of wrestling as a living cultural tradition. The show brings together historical objects, training equipment, and contemporary photography to create a dialogue about the sport's rituals and symbolism through November 1.

articles.headline: Review of Geetu Mohandas Film Toxic Starring Yash and Nayanthara
articles.summary: Geetu Mohandas's film 'Toxic', starring Yash, Nayanthara, and Kiara Advani, is described as a brash Indian action film with female characters. The review notes the film attempts to be transgressive but lacks shocking impact, ultimately characterizing the protagonist as 'toxic' rather than a villain.

articles.headline: Review of ONMO+ Smart Console for Cloud Gaming Ecosystems
articles.summary: The ONMO+ Smart Console offers an inexpensive entry into cloud gaming without being tied to specific hardware ecosystems. Bundled with a gaming controller, the platform can be used via web browsers or apps across multiple devices, including smartphones, tablets, and All-in-One PCs, freeing gamers from single-device constraints.

articles.headline: Indian Traditional Fermented Foods Offer Superior Gut Health Solutions
articles.summary: While packaged wellness solutions like kombucha are booming, traditional Indian kitchen staples like kanji, chaas, dahi, and pickles have long served gut health. These indigenous traditions, including fermented batters and soaked lentils, offer localized probiotic benefits that predate modern wellness branding.

articles.headline: Artist Yayoi Kusama Known for Polka Dotted Pumpkins Dies at 97
articles.summary: Avant-garde Japanese artist Yayoi Kusama has died at the age of 97. Famous for her polka-dotted sculptures and 'Infinity Mirrored Rooms', her work was inspired by vivid hallucinations and her lifelong battle with mental illness. Her installations at London’s Tate Modern ran for two years until 2023.

articles.headline: Columnist Explores Why Social Media Rewards Meaningless Outrage over Structure
articles.summary: Columnist Pooja Singh discusses how social media rewards fast, personal outrage—such as criticizing a brand advertisement—while structural issues like urban flooding and air quality fail to command sustained fury. The piece argues that instant gratification from online voice often ignores slow-moving environmental and social crises.

articles.headline: Profile of Matchbox Shots and Its Success in Indian Entertainment
articles.summary: Matchbox Shots, founded by Sanjay Routray, has emerged as a top production house with global hits like 'IC814: The Kandahar Hijack' and 'Operation Safed Sagar'. Following the success of 'Andhadhun', which grossed ₹450 crore, the boutique house emphasizes quality scripts and talent-led storytelling over traditional star power.

articles.headline: Comedian Conan O’Brien Visits India for New Travel Series
articles.summary: Comedian Conan O’Brien visited India for his series 'Conan O’Brien Must Go', now streaming on JioHotstar. The episode features O'Brien engaging in street cricket in Mumbai, visiting Dhobi Ghat, and meeting with local celebrities and residents, utilizing his trademark self-deprecating humor to explore Indian culture.

articles.headline: Kodaikanal Solar Observatory Marks 125 Years of Sun Observation
articles.summary: The Kodaikanal Solar Observatory (KSO) has maintained a continuous record of solar activities since 1899. Managed by the Indian Institute of Astrophysics, the facility is digitizing 34,000 images to help scientists predict space-weather conditions and understand the sun's magnetic fields and solar cycles.

articles.headline: Review of Book on Elon Musk Operating Philosophy and Ambition
articles.summary: A review of Eric Jorgenson’s 'The Book of Elon' analyzes Elon Musk's career from Zip2 to SpaceX and Tesla. The book is described as a curated collection of Musk's ideas, portraying him as a modern-day Edison focused on first principles and large-scale problem solving, while sometimes ignoring the operational and human costs of his methods.

articles.headline: Gulzar Reflects on Seventy Years as Partner and Muse to Mumbai
articles.summary: In his new book 'Aamchi Mumbai', 92-year-old poet Gulzar chronicles his seven-decade relationship with the city. From arriving at Bombay Central as a teenager to his time with the Progressive Writers Association, Gulzar uses poems and stories to record the city's shifting culture, infrastructure, and the quiet dignity of its people.

articles.headline: Raghavendra Rathore Argues Indian Craft Needs Design Relevance for Survival
articles.summary: Designer Raghavendra Rathore makes the case for reinventing Indian craft through intelligent design and global partnerships. He argues that traditional skills do not need rescuing, but rather opportunity and integration into modern lifestyle products to remain economically relevant for the millions who rely on them for livelihoods.

articles.headline: Sabyasachi Mukherjee Discusses Global Brand Expansion into Luxury Jewelry
articles.summary: Kolkata designer Sabyasachi Mukherjee is expanding his brand into high-end jewelry through a collaboration with New York’s Metropolitan Museum of Art. He outlines a business strategy focused on building a global luxury brand that prioritizes long-term investment value and consistent silhouettes over seasonal fashion trends.

articles.headline: Indigenous Forest Foods Revived Through Pop-ups and Subscription Boxes
articles.summary: Indigenous and wild foods like chambu and fiddlehead fern are finding new life through specialized foraging walks and subscription services. Organizations like NESFAS in Meghalaya and Spudnik Farms in Bengaluru are working with local communities to promote these climate-resilient, nutritious greens to urban consumers.

articles.headline: Standing in Food Queues Becomes Social Ritual and Status Symbol
articles.summary: Long lines at viral food outlets like Benne and LICK have transformed from marketing hurdles into social spaces and status signals for Gen Z diners. These queues offer rare opportunities for random social interaction and allow consumers to form personal opinions on 'it' foods in an era dominated by quick commerce and AI.

articles.headline: Seamus Murphy Photography Exhibition Life is in Many Days
articles.summary: Irish photographer Seamus Murphy’s work is on display at Museo Camera, Gurugram. The show, 'Life is in Many Days', features documentary images from Afghanistan, Gaza, Russia, the US, and Kolkata. Murphy's 'poetic realism' focuses on the everyday resilience and empathy of ordinary people living in conflict zones and transitionary periods.

articles.headline: Indian Families Share Challenges of Opening Ancestral Homes to Strangers
articles.summary: The rise of modern homestays across India involves families converting ancestral properties into retreats. Owners in regions like Himachal Pradesh, Goa, and Kerala discuss the operational realities of trading private sanctuary for hospitality, while preserving family recipes and cultural heritage as a sustainable livelihood.

articles.headline: Founders of NOTO Ice Cream Discuss Low Sugar Indulgence Business
articles.summary: Varun Sheth and Ashni Shah, founders of NOTO ice cream, discuss their journey in the low-sugar dessert market. Launched in 2019, the brand broke even in March with annual revenue reaching ₹35 crore in FY26. The founders focused on using polyols over high-potency sweeteners to appeal to health-conscious families and children.

articles.headline: Filmmaker Gurvinder Singh Traces Punjab’s Past in New Film Rehmat
articles.summary: Gurvinder Singh's new film 'Rehmat', which premiered at the Locarno Film Festival, uses three interconnected stories and historical houses to explore Punjab's turbulent history. Starring Naseeruddin Shah, the film focuses on themes of displacement, migration, and the enduring capacity for human compassion across generations.

articles.headline: Biopic Explores How Anthony Bourdain Integrated Politics into Food Programming
articles.summary: A new biopic titled 'Tony' dramatizes the early life of Anthony Bourdain. The film highlights how the late chef and documentarian revolutionized food travel shows by focusing on local kitchens, working-class stories, and political contexts, such as his critical coverage of US foreign policy in Lebanon and Cambodia.

articles.headline: Indian Auto Sector Seeks Alternatives to Restricted Chinese Technology
articles.summary: India's auto industry is diversifying away from Chinese technology due to Beijing's restrictions on rare earth magnet exports and battery tech transfers. Companies like Hero MotoCorp and JSW Group are adjusting supply chains or pausing gigafactory plans to explore alternative battery chemistries like NMC and non-restricted light rare earths.

articles.headline: Indian Equities End Week Lower Despite Foreign Buying of 30000 Crore
articles.summary: The Sensex and Nifty 50 closed marginally lower this week despite foreign institutional investors buying over ₹30,000 crore in August. Profit booking and a large pipeline of primary market issuances stalled secondary market momentum, though metal and IT stocks outperformed due to structural global demand and a US tech rally.

articles.headline: Death Toll from Nepal Flash Floods Crosses 570
articles.summary: The death toll from a flash flood on the Nepal-China border has exceeded 570 people. Authorities have warned of further flooding risks from a newly formed upstream lake. India’s external affairs ministry stated that 320 Indian nationals remain uncontactable following the disaster.

articles.headline: Yotta Data Services Eyes 20 Billion GPU Buildout for AI
articles.summary: Mumbai-based Yotta Data Services plans to deploy up to $20 billion in graphics processing units (GPUs) to meet surging global demand for AI computing. The company is boosting spending to expand computational resources as artificial intelligence workloads increase across industries.

articles.headline: Swiggy Instamart Focuses on Exclusive Products to Differentiate from Rivals
articles.summary: Swiggy Instamart is steering shoppers toward alternative brands and platform-exclusive products to distinguish itself in the quick-commerce market. Under its 'Switch to Better' initiative, it offers over 400 partner brands with preservative-free formulations, aiming to improve basket economics and capture new category growth.

articles.headline: NBFCs Sell More Retail Bad Loans to Asset Reconstruction Companies
articles.summary: Non-bank lenders are increasingly selling retail bad loans to asset reconstruction companies (ARCs) to clean balance sheets and free up capital. In FY26, retail loans comprised 35% of SRs issued, up from 25% in FY25, as stricter asset-quality rules and liquidity constraints drive NBFCs to resolve stressed exposures.

articles.headline: Algeria Becomes Third Largest LPG Source for India in August
articles.summary: Algeria has emerged as India's third-largest LPG supplier, sending 110,711 tonnes in August. The shift follows disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz. State-owned IOC has finalized a deal to buy 55,000 mt per month in 2027 as India seeks to diversify energy sources beyond West Asia.

articles.headline: India July Industrial Growth Records Seven Point Three Percent Rise
articles.summary: India's industrial output (IIP) grew 6.7% year-on-year in July, driven primarily by a 7.3% rise in manufacturing. Electricity generation grew 8.7%, while mining output saw a marginal contraction of 0.9%. The data marks the fourth release under the new 2022-23 base year series.

articles.headline: FirstCry CEO Predicts Casualties in Niche Quick Commerce Platforms
articles.summary: FirstCry CEO Supam Maheshwari expects fatalities among specialty quick-commerce platforms due to high logistics and customer acquisition costs. He argues that large retailers with established store networks and private labels are better positioned to achieve profitability compared to niche startups building from scratch.

articles.headline: Fireflies AI Targets Acquisitions of Indian Application Layer Startups
articles.summary: AI unicorn Fireflies AI is looking to acquire Indian startups focusing on voice AI and application-layer work automation. CEO Krish Ramineni noted the resourcefulness of Indian entrepreneurs in controlling costs and using open-source models, as M&A deals in the Indian AI space have already hit $980 million in 2026.

articles.headline: Executive Coaching Industry Faces Competition from New Entrants and AI
articles.summary: India's executive coaching industry is seeing downward fee pressure as a wave of new coaches and AI-enabled matchmaking platforms enter the market. CXO coaches can charge up to ₹1 lakh per hour, but the rise of advice bots and a crowded field of credentialed professionals is forcing many to lower rates to secure corporate engagements.

articles.headline: Congress alleges government pressure as publisher pulls out of Sonia Gandhi memoir
articles.summary: A controversy has erupted after Penguin Random House reportedly withdrew from publishing Sonia Gandhi’s memoir, 'Belonging'. The Congress party claimed government pressure forced the decision, calling it a "murder of democracy." The RSS-linked journal Organiser had previously criticized the book for its content. The publisher has not issued a final statement on the matter.

articles.headline: Supreme Court upholds Karnataka government's order on state anthem duration
articles.summary: The Supreme Court has refused to interfere with a Karnataka High Court order upholding the state government’s 2022 decision to prescribe a specific duration of two minutes and 30 seconds for the state anthem, 'Jaya Bharata Jananiya Tanujate'. The court ruled that the state has the prerogative to fix the time and duration for rendering the anthem.

articles.headline: Karnataka minister B Nagendra resigns over Rs 89-crore tribal corporation scam
articles.summary: Scheduled Tribes Welfare Minister B Nagendra has resigned from the Karnataka cabinet following allegations of a multi-crore scam at the Karnataka Maharshi Valmiki ST Development Corporation. The scam involves the illegal transfer of nearly Rs 89 crore to various bank accounts. Nagendra stated he resigned voluntarily to ensure a fair investigation by the SIT and central agencies.

articles.headline: Pragg becomes first Indian to win GCT title, pockets $200,000 prize
articles.summary: Indian Grandmaster R Praggnanandhaa made history by becoming the first player from India to win the prestigious Grand Chess Tour (GCT) title. He secured the victory after a dramatic final day in St Louis, staging a massive comeback against defending champion Fabiano Caruana. The 21-year-old earned a $200,000 prize for his performance across the five-event series.

articles.headline: Bescom staff face locked gates in Bengaluru Gruha Jyothi verification drive
articles.summary: The verification drive for the Gruha Jyothi free electricity scheme is facing hurdles in Bengaluru as many gated communities and apartments are denying entry to Bescom officials. Despite 2.1 crore consumers being eligible across Karnataka, over 1.2 crore have been verified. Officials cite security concerns by residents as the main reason for the slowdown in verification.

articles.headline: Bengaluru auto and taxi unions demand action against illegal bike taxi apps
articles.summary: Federations of auto and taxi drivers in Bengaluru have petitioned the transport department to remove mobile applications of bike-taxi aggregators. The unions allege these services operate without a legal framework, leading to unfair competition and safety concerns for passengers. They have issued a 15-day deadline for government action, threatening protests and black-flag demonstrations.

articles.headline: NSG conducts specialized anti-terror crash course for 500 Bengaluru police personnel
articles.summary: The National Security Guard (NSG) has launched a month-long training program for 500 Bengaluru police personnel to enhance city security. The training covers counter-terrorism, hostage rescue, sniper operations, and bomb disposal. Personnel from various local units, including the Internal Security Division, will undergo this intensive training to improve response capabilities.

articles.headline: Citizens launch postcard campaign against Hebbal-Silk Board tunnel road project
articles.summary: Environmentalists and activists in Bengaluru have started a postcard campaign urging the state government to scrap the proposed 17km Hebbal-Silk Board tunnel road. The project, estimated to cost Rs 17,698 crore, is criticized for its potential impact on Lalbagh Botanical Garden and local parks. Citizens are mailing postcards to the Chief Minister demanding more sustainable transport solutions.

articles.headline: Deputy CM Shivakumar urges cabinet sub-committee to review private school fees
articles.summary: Karnataka Deputy CM DK Shivakumar has directed a cabinet sub-committee to examine the rising costs of private school education. Middle-class families are reportedly struggling with hike in fees, vendor-tied books, and uniforms. The committee will look into implementing regulatory reforms to control fee structures and ensure education remains affordable for all sections of society.

articles.headline: HD Kumaraswamy alleges irregularities in KPSC recruitment for rural development posts
articles.summary: Union Minister HD Kumaraswamy has alleged a new recruitment scam in the Karnataka Public Service Commission (KPSC) regarding Assistant Executive Engineer (AEE) posts. He claims that OMR sheets were tampered with and manipulated to favor certain candidates. The state government has formed a sub-committee to investigate these allegations and verify examination records.

articles.headline: Eight men sentenced to life imprisonment for 2017 murder in Bengaluru
articles.summary: A local court in Bengaluru has sentenced eight men to life imprisonment for the 2017 murder of a 32-year-old man, Harish. The victim was attacked with machetes after he had scolded the accused for smoking in public. The court relied on eyewitness testimony and medical evidence to convict the group. The judge highlighted the brutal nature of the crime committed in broad daylight.

articles.headline: FDA inspects Bengaluru venue ahead of unapproved peptide party event
articles.summary: The Food Safety and Drug Administration (FDA) in Bengaluru called off a scheduled "peptide party" after an inspection revealed the use of unapproved and expired substances. Peptide parties involve informal gatherings where individuals use supplements for fitness or anti-aging. The FDA seized several packets of expired milk and unauthorized chemical products from the venue's kitchen.

articles.headline: High Court orders 3 lakh compensation for illegal arrest before notice expiry
articles.summary: The Karnataka High Court has ordered an investigating officer to pay Rs 3 lakh as compensation to a person arrested before the expiry of a court-issued notice period. The court emphasized that police cannot treat citizens with whim and must respect procedural safeguards. The compensation will be borne by the state, with the option to recover it from the erring officer.

articles.headline: CID grills IAS officer Gnanendra Kumar over KPSC examination irregularities
articles.summary: The Criminal Investigation Department (CID) questioned IAS officer Gnanendra Kumar for over nine hours regarding alleged irregularities in KPSC recruitment exams. The probe follows a raid on his residence where investigators reportedly found incriminating documents and evidence of OMR sheet tampering. The CID is investigating the extent of his involvement in the recruitment scam.

articles.headline: CAG report reveals 43% of Karnataka rain gauges are non-functional
articles.summary: A report by the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) has found that 43% of telemetry rain gauges and weather stations in Karnataka were not working as of late 2023. This massive failure in the data collection network has compromised the state's ability to accurately assess rainfall, forecast floods, and plan for drought management, leaving many areas without reliable weather data.

articles.headline: Students stranded as colleges allotted through KEA found to be closed
articles.summary: Several students in Karnataka are in distress after discovering that colleges they were allotted by the Karnataka Examinations Authority (KEA) are actually shut down or non-existent. Complaints have surfaced about fake addresses and lack of infrastructure at multiple institutes. The KEA has promised to investigate these cases and provide alternative college seats to affected students.

articles.headline: Uttar Pradesh reports first swine flu death of the season in Lucknow
articles.summary: Lucknow has recorded its first death due to the H1N1 (swine flu) virus this season. A 50-year-old woman succumbed to the infection at a city hospital after being admitted with severe respiratory symptoms. Health officials have issued an alert and are conducting screenings for high-risk individuals. Public hospitals have been directed to set up isolated wards for potential cases.

articles.headline: Central government to send 840 tonnes of onion to Delhi to stabilize prices
articles.summary: The central government will dispatch a buffer stock of 840 tonnes of onions from Nashik to Delhi to control rising retail prices. Onions will be sold at subsidized rates of Rs 35 per kg through cooperatives. Retail prices in the capital have recently surged to over Rs 60 per kg. This move is part of an effort to provide relief to consumers amid supply chain disruptions.

articles.headline: Enforcement Directorate probes foreign remittance deal linked to Lionel Messi's Kerala visit
articles.summary: The Enforcement Directorate (ED) has launched an investigation into potential FEMA violations regarding a foreign remittance deal associated with a proposed visit by football legend Lionel Messi to Kerala. The probe centers on the financial transactions of organizers and sponsors involved in the 2022 World Cup-winning team's trip, following reports of procedural lapses.

articles.headline: Rehabilitated former Maoists celebrate Raksha Bandhan with Gadchiroli police
articles.summary: In a significant gesture of reconciliation, women former Maoist rebels tied rakhis to police personnel in Gadchiroli, Maharashtra. These women, who were once involved in several violent ambushes, have surrendered and joined the mainstream through government rehabilitation programs. The event highlights the success of community policing and anti-insurgency efforts in tribal regions.

articles.headline: Rescue operations in Nepal disrupted by fresh avalanches and overflowing lakes
articles.summary: Rescue efforts at the Nepal-Tibet border were halted on Friday as a new unstable barrier lake began overflowing, triggering a fresh avalanche. Massive amounts of debris and mud have clogged river valleys, making it impossible for ground teams to reach isolated sites. Authorities have deployed helicopters for aerial surveys, but heavy rain continues to hamper safety and visibility.

articles.headline: Record 5.3 million dollar fee paid for Panama Canal transit during drought
articles.summary: A shipping tanker has paid a record $5.3 million in a last-minute auction to secure a transit slot through the Panama Canal. The high price is a result of extreme drought conditions caused by El Niño, which has led to severe water level drops and reduced the number of daily transits allowed. This situation has caused massive shipping backlogs and increased global transport costs.

articles.headline: US court rules Pentagon's ban on Anthropic AI software was unlawful
articles.summary: A US district court has ruled that the Pentagon’s decision to ban the use of Anthropic’s AI chatbot software was legally flawed. The judge stated that the Department of Defense failed to provide adequate justification for its "arbitrary" claim that the software posed a national security risk. The ruling is a significant victory for AI companies challenging government restrictions on technology.

articles.headline: Russian-speaking cyber-criminals hack seven global firms using AI tools
articles.summary: A report by cybersecurity firms reveals that a group of Russian-speaking hackers successfully compromised the networks of seven international companies using advanced AI assistants. The hackers used AI to generate highly convincing phishing emails and exploit software vulnerabilities. This marks one of the first documented cases of large-scale corporate cyberattacks powered by generative AI.

articles.headline: England seamers dominate Pakistan on opening day of Lord's Test match
articles.summary: England's pace bowlers took full control on the first day of the second Test at Lord's, dismissing Pakistan for just 108 runs. Ollie Robinson led the attack with four wickets, while Jofra Archer made a successful return with two crucial breakthroughs. By the end of play, England reached 220 for 4, securing a significant 112-run lead with six first-innings wickets remaining.

articles.headline: Gujarat government launches DNA profiling to identify future sporting champions
articles.summary: The Gujarat government has introduced a pioneering program using DNA analysis to identify and train potential elite athletes. The project involves analyzing genetic data from over 2,000 children to match their physiological traits with specific Olympic sports. The initiative aims to provide scientific training and nutritional support to help India become a global sporting powerhouse.

articles.headline: CJI Chandrachud says clean energy push is unfair to developing nations
articles.summary: Chief Justice of India DY Chandrachud stated that industrialized nations are placing an unfair burden on developing countries regarding the transition to clean energy. He argued that developed countries, which have historically benefited from fossil fuels, must provide financial and technological support to ensure a just transition. He emphasized that global environmental responsibility must be balanced.

articles.headline: Cipla's Pune manufacturing unit loses drug sale licenses after FDA inspection
articles.summary: The Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has cancelled the drug sale licenses for Cipla's manufacturing facility in Pune following a series of regulatory violations. Inspections revealed discrepancies in storage conditions and lapses in maintaining proper batch records for certain medications. The company has been ordered to immediately recall the affected batches from the market for public safety.

articles.headline: Chinese humanoid robots break sprint records at Beijing Robot Games
articles.summary: A humanoid robot developed by a Beijing-based tech firm has set a new world record by completing a 100-meter sprint in just 9.39 seconds. This performance beats the human world record held by Usain Bolt. The Beijing Humanoid Robot Games featured over 2,000 robots competing in various events like high jump and soccer, showcasing rapid advancements in bipedal robotics and AI.

articles.headline: FDA issues notices to Shah Rukh Khan, Ajay Devgn over advertising
articles.summary: The Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has issued notices to Bollywood stars Shah Rukh Khan, Ajay Devgn, and Tiger Shroff for appearing in controversial advertisements. The notices concern potential violations related to surrogate advertising for tobacco-linked products. The actors have been given seven days to respond to the inquiry regarding their endorsement deals and compliance with norms.

articles.headline: Hansal Mehta produced film Birds in the Dark to premiere at BIFF
articles.summary: The Punjabi film 'Birds in the Dark', produced by renowned filmmaker Hansal Mehta, has been selected for its world premiere at the 31st Busan International Film Festival (BIFF). Directed by Sahil Sai, the film explores themes of gender, caste, and societal expectations in rural India. The selection marks Mehta’s third outing at the prestigious international festival in South Korea.

articles.headline: Rakul Preet Singh to play Surpanakha in Nitesh Tiwari's Ramayana trilogy
articles.summary: Actress Rakul Preet Singh has confirmed her role as Surpanakha in Nitesh Tiwari's upcoming high-budget Ramayana film trilogy. She will be joining a star-studded cast including Ranbir Kapoor and Sai Pallavi. Rakul stated that the role offers a complex character arc with multiple layers, and she is looking forward to portraying a unique interpretation of the historical antagonist.

articles.headline: Telugu actor and producer GV Narayana Rao passes away at 73
articles.summary: Veteran Telugu actor and producer GV Narayana Rao died on Thursday in Hyderabad at the age of 73 following a cardiac arrest. Known for his roles in classic films like 'Anthuleni Katha', he was a respected figure in the South Indian film industry. Several prominent actors and politicians expressed their condolences, highlighting his contribution to Telugu cinema over four decades.

articles.headline: Kari Bazaar to bring master artisans from 26 states to Bengaluru
articles.summary: The 'Kari Bazaar' exhibition is set to open in Bengaluru, featuring over 250 master craftsmen and award-winning artisans from across India. The 11-day event will showcase traditional handlooms, pottery, jewelry, and sustainable products from 26 states. The bazaar aims to provide a direct platform for rural artisans to interact with urban consumers and keep traditional crafts alive.

articles.headline: NTA and Nilekani panel seek public ideas for major exam overhaul
articles.summary: A high-power committee headed by Nandan Nilekani has invited public suggestions for comprehensive reforms to India’s examination system. The panel, formed following recent leaks, aims to make national tests like NEET-UG more secure and transparent. Suggestions can be submitted via a dedicated website or WhatsApp till September 30, focusing on technological solutions and institutional changes.

articles.headline: Punjab youth arrested for spying and providing live CCTV feeds to Pakistan
articles.summary: A 20-year-old man from Jalandhar, Punjab, has been arrested for allegedly spying for Pakistan's ISI. The accused had installed CCTV cameras at strategic border locations and provided live video feeds to his handlers across the border. Police seized spying equipment and mobile phones used to transmit sensitive data. This is the third such espionage case reported in the border region recently.

articles.headline: Puducherry CM Rangasamy threatens to resign if statehood is not granted
articles.summary: Puducherry Chief Minister N Rangasamy has stated that he is prepared to step down from his post if the central government does not grant full statehood to the Union Territory. He claimed that the current administrative structure hinders his government's ability to implement welfare schemes and projects effectively. His remarks have sparked a fresh debate on the political status of Puducherry.

articles.headline: Madras High Court rules minister cannot refuse to appear in court
articles.summary: The Madras High Court has ruled that Tamil Nadu minister Wilson must appear before a trial court in connection with a criminal case. The court rejected his plea for exemption, stating that being a minister does not grant him the status of a king who is above the law. The case relates to a 2022 incident involving an alleged assault on his brother-in-law and sister-in-law.

articles.headline: Centre informs HC that Advocates Act does not bar convict's entry
articles.summary: The central government told the Madras High Court that there is no specific bar in the Advocates Act preventing a person who has previously faced a death sentence or life imprisonment from enrolling as an advocate. This submission came during a hearing regarding the enrollment plea of Rajiv Gandhi assassination convict AG Perarivalan. The court is considering the statutory balance for rehabilitation.

articles.headline: Former Rajasthan CM Gehlot questions why truth is hidden in Sonia memoir
articles.summary: Former Rajasthan Chief Minister Ashok Gehlot has questioned the reported withdrawal of Sonia Gandhi's memoir by its publisher. He asked why the public is being deprived of reading a book that details the former Congress president's journey and political life. Gehlot alleged that government pressure on publishers is stifling free speech and preventing the documentation of modern Indian history.

articles.headline: Stampede at UP mayor's Rakhi event leaves one woman dead, several injured
articles.summary: A 45-year-old woman died and three others were injured during a stampede at a Raksha Bandhan event organized by the Bareilly mayor in Uttar Pradesh. The tragedy occurred when a large crowd rushed to collect gift hampers and food packets. Police have registered a case for negligence against the event organizers, and an inquiry has been ordered into the lack of crowd control measures.

articles.headline: Mumbai woman ends life after 1.5 crore fraud using forged documents
articles.summary: A 38-year-old woman from Dombivli, Mumbai, committed suicide after discovering that a bank account in her name was used for fraudulent transactions worth Rs 1.5 crore. The victim was reportedly unaware that her documents were forged to open the account, which was used for cybercrimes and money laundering. Police are investigating the involvement of bank officials and a local cyber-fraud syndicate.

articles.headline: Ford to hire 500 professionals for its global capability center in India
articles.summary: Ford Business Solutions (FBS) has announced plans to hire 500 professionals in India by 2027 to strengthen its global capability center. The hiring will focus on advanced technology roles in AI, data science, and connected vehicles. This move highlights India's growing importance as a global hub for automotive engineering and software development, supporting Ford's digital transformation goals.

articles.headline: US commander reports Strait of Hormuz shipping lanes are mine-free
articles.summary: A top US naval commander for the Middle East has confirmed that the international shipping lanes in the Strait of Hormuz are currently free of mines. The statement follows several months of intensive patrolling and mine-sweeping operations by US and allied forces in response to regional tensions. This update provides much-needed assurance for global oil and gas transporters using the strategic waterway.

articles.headline: BCCI stance on National Sports Bill creates confusion within cricket board
articles.summary: The BCCI's recent affidavit in the Odisha High Court has created confusion regarding its stance on the National Sports Governance Bill. While the board previously claimed it is not a "designated sport" under the act, it is now seeking government-prescribed rules for its internal elections. State cricket associations are reportedly unclear about whether to follow the board’s previous mandate or new court-driven directives.

articles.headline: Union Minister Jual Oram alleges smear campaign to topple tribal leadership
articles.summary: Union Tribal Affairs Minister Jual Oram has alleged that a "smear campaign" is being run by political opponents to tarnish his reputation and topple his leadership. Speaking in Bhubaneswar, Oram claimed that baseless allegations of corruption are being spread to create discord within his tribal base. He vowed to fight back and continue working for the development of tribal communities across India.

articles.headline: Expert warns of ten everyday habits that can increase heart risk
articles.summary: A leading cardiologist has identified ten common daily habits that significantly increase the risk of heart disease, including skipping breakfast and excessive screen time at night. Other risk factors mentioned include high sugary beverage consumption, social isolation, and neglected dental hygiene. The expert advised regular health check-ups and simple lifestyle adjustments to maintain long-term cardiovascular health.

articles.headline: Vibrant murals by international artists reclaim streets of El Salvador
articles.summary: Artists from across Latin America have transformed several towns in El Salvador into vibrant outdoor galleries as part of the Pigmen Trip Festival. Over 200 murals featuring bold colors and striking imagery have been painted to promote culture, freedom, and sustainability. The initiative aims to revitalize public spaces and use art as a tool for social change and community development.

articles.headline: Industrial growth slowed to 6.7% in July
articles.summary: India's industrial output growth eased to 6.7% in July, down from 7.3% in June, primarily due to a slowdown in the mining sector, which contracted by 0.9%. Manufacturing, however, showed resilience with 7.3% growth, driven by strong performance in sectors like automotive and electrical equipment. Overall industrial activity was supported by a robust electricity and gas supply sector.

articles.headline: Subhash Chandra disputes ‘haircut’, says group’s debts repaid
articles.summary: Zee Group Founder Subhash Chandra challenged allegations of financial wrongdoing, stating his group has repaid most of its debts. He plans to visit Switzerland for investment work. Chandra claimed his group has repaid around ₹43,000 crore of its ₹45,000 crore outstanding debt, refuting claims of massive personal wealth.

articles.headline: Cakes, flowers and pets reinvent Raksha Bandhan
articles.summary: Raksha Bandhan is evolving into a broader consumption occasion, with retailers now monetising expanded spending baskets. Online marketplaces and specialist pet-care brands are offering pet-friendly items, while bakers, florists, and jewellers are bundling gifts with rakhis. The festival is expected to generate ₹30,000-32,000 crore in trade nationally.

articles.headline: ED freezes deposits worth ₹52 crore in DHFL case
articles.summary: The Enforcement Directorate (ED) has frozen bank deposits worth ₹51.75 crore in connection with a bank loan fraud case involving DHFL. The ED probe stems from a CBI FIR filed on a complaint from a consortium of 17 banks against DHFL and its promoters. This action is part of the ongoing investigation into alleged money laundering.

articles.headline: REIT fundraising soars in FY26, InvIT collections dip 21%
articles.summary: Fundraising through Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs) nearly doubled to ₹9,300 crore in FY26, with the average issue size increasing by 31%. Conversely, Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs) saw fundraising decline by 21% to ₹21,026 crore, despite an increase in the number of issues, indicating a trend towards smaller transactions.

articles.headline: Indian automakers eye easier access to Chinese parts, EV tech
articles.summary: The gradual improvement in India-China relations is raising hopes for easier access to Chinese automotive components and EV technology. Indian automakers are increasingly dependent on China for battery cells and critical electricals. The industry is closely watching President Xi Jinping's expected visit for potential policy easing.

articles.headline: JSW MG Motor India seeks lower taxes on plug-in hybrid EVs
articles.summary: JSW MG Motor India has called for lower taxation on plug-in hybrid vehicles (PHEVs), suggesting an 18% tax rate instead of the current 28%. The company plans to introduce extended-range EVs to India, seeing PHEVs as a bridge technology for consumers transitioning to electric mobility. This move aims to make EVs more accessible and affordable.

articles.headline: India not inclined to make proposed US H-1B fee hike a bilateral issue
articles.summary: India is unlikely to escalate the proposed US H-1B visa fee hike into a bilateral issue, viewing it as a commercial matter for US employers. While the fee increase will significantly impact Indian IT firms, New Delhi acknowledges US visa policy as a sovereign domain. Historically, India has discussed visa issues with the US.

articles.headline: Venezuela mulls OPEC exit as US discusses oil fields stake
articles.summary: Venezuela is considering withdrawing from OPEC, potentially impacting the oil cartel. This comes as the US discusses taking a significant stake in Venezuela's oil fields. The potential exit follows a shift in US-Venezuela relations since the Trump administration took control of the nation's oil sales.

articles.headline: FCNR (B) inflows drive forex reserves to new high of $729.32 bn
articles.summary: India's foreign exchange reserves reached an all-time high of $729.328 billion in the week ended August 21, boosted by robust inflows into foreign currency non-resident deposits. Since March-end 2026, reserves have increased by $38.221 billion, strengthening India's external shock absorption capacity.

articles.headline: Trump administration seeks to restrict internships for international students
articles.summary: The Trump administration has issued a memo to universities seeking to restrict Curricular Practical Training (CPT) authorisations for international students. Colleges not complying may lose certification. This move aims to tighten curbs on CPT, impacting Indian students and universities.

articles.headline: In 5 months of FY27, govt mops up more than 3/4th of BE under MCR
articles.summary: The government has collected over three-fourths of its budget estimates under Miscellaneous Capital Receipts (MCR) in the first five months of FY27. MCR includes proceeds from share sales and asset monetisation. The government aims to collect ₹80,000 crore under MCR for FY27.

articles.headline: Land Rover Defender Trophy Edition revives Camel Trophy spirit
articles.summary: The Land Rover Defender Trophy Edition, exclusively for the Defender 110 variant with a 3.0-litre inline-six diesel engine, pays homage to the iconic Camel Trophy era. It features a distinctive yellow paint scheme, purposeful 20-inch steel rims, and various add-ons, offering exceptional off-road presence and refined driving dynamics.

articles.headline: All-new Pulsar 125 and 150 mark 25 years of the brand
articles.summary: Bajaj has launched the all-new Pulsar 125 and Pulsar 150 motorcycles to celebrate the brand's 25th anniversary. These models feature new technology, engines, gearboxes, chassis, and modernised bodywork. The Pulsar 125 is priced at ₹92,990, while the Pulsar 150 ranges from ₹1.15 lakh to ₹1.23 lakh.

articles.headline: Honda Rebel 300 makes India debut at ₹2.22 lakh
articles.summary: The Honda Rebel 300 has been launched in India at ₹2.22 lakh for the standard variant. It features a 286 cc single-cylinder engine and a 6-speed gearbox. An e-clutch variant is also available, priced at ₹2.62 lakh. The Rebel 300 is a highly anticipated motorcycle in the Indian market.

articles.headline: BMW launches the X1 LWB in India with more comfort
articles.summary: BMW has launched the long-wheelbase version of the fourth-generation X1 in India at ₹49.9 lakh. The X1 LWB offers enhanced backseat comfort and features, available exclusively with a 1.5-litre petrol engine. It serves as the entry point into the X1 range, competing with other premium compact SUVs.

articles.headline: Mercedes-Benz E220d: understated elegance for business travel
articles.summary: The Mercedes-Benz E220d offers understated elegance and comfort, ideal for business travel. Its quiet cabin, refined diesel engine, and smooth ride create a luxurious experience. The E-Class prioritises comfort over sportiness, making it a practical and endearing choice for discerning buyers.

articles.headline: IT stocks aid Nifty recovery, focus on Fed Chair’s cues
articles.summary: Domestic IT stocks surged, led by TCS, Tech Mahindra, and Infosys, following Nvidia's strong results. The Nifty IT index gained 3.5%. The market focus now shifts to Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh's remarks at the Jackson Hole symposium. Nifty closed higher, driven by sector-specific gains.

articles.headline: SEBI issues observations on NSE’s IPO draft papers
articles.summary: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) has issued observations on the National Stock Exchange's (NSE) draft IPO papers. This update comes after SEBI's in-principle approval to settle co-location and dark fibre matters for ₹1,491.21 crore. The NSE's IPO is expected to be one of the largest by size.

articles.headline: Tempsens clocks biggest listing gain of 110% in 2026, closes at ₹586.65
articles.summary: Tempsens Instruments' shares jumped over 110% to ₹631.2 on their market debut against an IPO price of ₹300. The company's strong performance reflects its category leadership and financial growth. Tempsens cautioned that the sharp rise pushed valuations significantly above historical averages.

articles.headline: Annu Projects IPO subscribed nearly 3x, others get SEBI nod
articles.summary: Annu Projects IPO was subscribed 2.93 times, led by non-institutional investors. Separately, four companies - Bharat PET, Sadbhav EPC, Paras Healthcare, and MK Sons Fine Jewels - received SEBI's clearance to float their IPOs. The IPO market is seeing a strong return of niche players.

articles.headline: AI: Where does the money go?
articles.summary: India's Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) spending hit a record ₹40,794 crore in 2024-25, up 17%. However, richer states and sectors like education, where public provision is strong, receive the bulk of funds. The article argues for directing CSR spending towards areas with greater need, suggesting a mismatch between wealth and need.

articles.headline: Smart glasses are offensive and should be banned
articles.summary: The use of smart glasses with embedded cameras raises serious privacy concerns, including covert recording and potential misuse. India's Digital Personal Data Protection framework is still under phased implementation. The article calls for policymakers to act swiftly to stop the sale of such devices, citing privacy risks and lack of effective safeguards.

articles.headline: What’s wrong in using AI to write articles, asks ChatGPT
articles.summary: The article explores the debate around AI-written articles, arguing that AI can assist journalists by handling routine tasks, freeing them for more in-depth reporting. It emphasizes that the quality, usefulness, and interest of an article, determined by human editors, are paramount, not whether AI was involved in the first draft.

articles.headline: You’re living longer, Americans
articles.summary: American life expectancy hit a record 79 years in 2024, surpassing the pre-pandemic high. This increase reflects improvements in public health and a decrease in deaths from major causes. The statistic indicates a positive trend in the overall well-being of the US population.

articles.headline: El Nino shock may result in food inflation, supply chain risks
articles.summary: An early-onset, high-intensity El Nino event could create macroeconomic shocks, impacting agricultural markets, shipping, energy, and inflation. Commodities like sugar, cocoa, and palm oil may face price pressure. Central banks may need to reassess monetary policy due to potential food price shocks.

articles.headline: 40% fall in ADAS hardware cost brings safety tech closer to mass-market cars
articles.summary: The cost of ADAS hardware has fallen by approximately 40% in 12 months, making safety features like automatic emergency braking and adaptive cruise control more accessible in mass-market cars. Falling prices of LiDAR, cameras, and radar modules allow automakers to offer these technologies on higher-volume models.

articles.headline: Airtel gains 26.8 lakh users in July, Reliance Jio adds 24.4 lakh
articles.summary: Bharti Airtel added 26.8 lakh mobile subscribers in July, while Reliance Jio gained 24.4 lakh users. Vodafone Idea also saw net additions. The Indian wireless market expanded by 55.38 lakh subscribers, reaching a total of 128.79 crore.

articles.headline: RBI to conduct 6 trillion rupee VRRR auction to soak liquidity
articles.summary: The RBI will conduct its highest-ever 15-day variable rate reverse repo (VRRR) auction of 6 trillion rupees on August 31. This aims to absorb surplus liquidity from the banking system, which stood at 3.75 trillion rupees on Thursday. The move is considered a less painful way to manage liquidity compared to adjusting the cash reserve ratio.

articles.headline: Emissions breach may force two-wheelers into limp home mode
articles.summary: The road transport ministry and the two-wheeler industry are developing a mechanism to put vehicles into 'limp-home mode' if emissions exceed BS6 OBD-II thresholds. Under this mode, vehicle power or speed would be restricted to force repairs. While industry bodies requested a delay until BS7 in 2027, the government insisted on implementation for vehicles made from April 2025.

articles.headline: Vodafone Idea records sixth straight month of subscriber gains
articles.summary: Vodafone Idea (Vi) added 240,114 customers in July, marking its sixth consecutive month of net subscriber growth. The carrier’s base reached 199.06 million, nearing the 200 million milestone. This reversal follows years of losses and coincides with network investments and the rollout of 5G services in major cities.

articles.headline: RBI forex strategy shifts from crisis management to record reserves
articles.summary: India's foreign exchange reserves hit an all-time high of $729.3 billion in August 2026, a sharp rise from just $1.2 billion during the 1991 balance-of-payments crisis. The evolution of forex management since liberalisation has moved the country from a fixed exchange rate to a market-determined system with one of the world's largest reserve buffers.

articles.headline: Ola Electric launches S1Z scooter with homegrown battery technology
articles.summary: Ola Electric introduced the S1Z scooter range, its first to use locally developed Bharat Cell LFP (lithium ferro phosphate) battery technology. Priced at 79,999 and 99,999 rupees, the variants offer ranges of up to 179 km and 301 km. The move aims to lower battery costs through vertical integration and in-house manufacturing.

articles.headline: Subhash Chandra seeks independent audit to examine Essel debt
articles.summary: Essel group founder Subhash Chandra claimed the group has repaid 43,000 crore of its 45,000 crore debt. He urged Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman to appoint an independent auditor to review borrowings and repayments. Chandra contested NCLT claims of a 22,000 crore liability, stating the actual remaining amount is around 3,900 crore.

articles.headline: Maharashtra FDA cancels Cipla warehouse licences over packaging violations
articles.summary: The Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration cancelled the drug sale licences of a Cipla warehouse in Pune. The regulator cited unauthorized promotional text on the packaging of Reactin Plus Tablets and seized stock worth 11.19 lakh rupees. Cipla has contested the order, stating the matter is currently sub judice.

articles.headline: Zee Entertainment bets on sports and animation for growth
articles.summary: Zee Entertainment Enterprises Ltd (ZEEL) plans to invest in sports, animation, VFX, and digital media to build new growth engines. CEO Punit Goenka stated that these new-age segments are increasingly driving the media landscape. The company aims to diversify its portfolio beyond traditional businesses to capture a larger share of the evolving market.

articles.headline: Recovery from personal guarantors remains low at one percent
articles.summary: Data from the IBBI shows that lenders recovered only 234.56 crore rupees from personal guarantors by June 2026, representing just 1% of total admitted claims. Legal experts suggest a structural flaw in the IBC framework, as repayment plans are often debtor-proposed settlements rather than court-enforced obligations, limiting creditor leverage.

articles.headline: AI deployment helps logistics firms reduce failed delivery rates
articles.summary: Artificial intelligence is becoming essential for logistics firms, helping direct-to-consumer and e-commerce brands reduce failed deliveries by up to 20%. Tools like AI voice agents and address verification engines have cut return-to-origin (RTO) rates significantly. Startups like MyMuse reported resolving 80% of non-delivery cases within a day using AI.

articles.headline: New technologies will create more jobs, says Vice-President
articles.summary: Vice-President C P Radhakrishnan stated that AI and new technologies will enhance the ease of doing work and create more jobs, comparing the current shift to the introduction of computers. Speaking at the launch of the Gnani Artha AI stack, he dismissed concerns about job losses, noting that the IT industry has historically been a major job creator.

articles.headline: Anthropic discusses buying AI chip startup MatX for 7 billion dollars
articles.summary: AI lab Anthropic reportedly discussed acquiring custom chip startup MatX for roughly $7 billion to accelerate its in-house hardware development. While acquisition talks are no longer active, the discussions have shifted toward a partnership. MatX, founded by former Google engineers, is currently seeking capital at a $4 billion valuation.

articles.headline: Govt targets faster conversion of polluting trucks in Delhi-NCR
articles.summary: The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways expects to convert 223,000 old trucks and buses in the NCR to cleaner fuels in one year, twice as fast as initially planned. The Parivartan scheme, launched in June, facilitates the replacement of BS-IV vehicles with BS-VI or electric alternatives to curb pollution in the national capital region.

articles.headline: Finance Ministry starts FY28 Budget exercise with realistic projections
articles.summary: The Ministry of Finance has begun the Union Budget exercise for FY28, urging ministries to provide realistic revised estimates for FY27 and estimates for the next year. The move seeks to avoid frequent mid-year re-appropriations. Consultations with agriculture and industry stakeholders are scheduled to start from October 12, 2026.

articles.headline: MCA likely to reduce mandatory cooling-off period for auditors
articles.summary: The Ministry of Corporate Affairs is considering reducing the proposed three-year cooling-off period for auditors to one year. Instead of a blanket ban on all non-audit services, the ministry may only restrict a specific list of prohibited services. The change follows industry pressure and recommendations from a joint committee of Parliament.

articles.headline: Sugar mills to receive fortnightly sale quotas from September
articles.summary: The government will allocate fortnightly sugar sale quotas to mills from September to ensure smooth supply and prevent artificial scarcity. The decision follows a physical verification of stocks which revealed some mills held more sugar than declared. Retail sugar prices have recently eased with ex-mill rates falling by 20%.

articles.headline: Indian tyre exports surge 16 percent to 7,700 crore in Q1
articles.summary: Tyre exports from India grew 16% year-on-year to 7,700 crore rupees in the first quarter of FY27. This follows a record export value of 27,312 crore in the previous financial year. Export of passenger car radial tyres saw a 21% increase, indicating a strong start for the sector despite geopolitical and logistics challenges.

articles.headline: CII taskforce suggests new green financing institution for India
articles.summary: A CII taskforce led by Jayant Sinha has proposed a dedicated green finance institution to catalyze $1 trillion in climate investments over 10 years. The report calls for a climate finance taxonomy and streamlining sustainability reporting. India needs an estimated $100-125 billion annually to stay on its 2070 net-zero trajectory.

articles.headline: Flood spending falls in vulnerable states despite rising disaster risks
articles.summary: India's share of global disasters has remained steady, but state expenditure on floods and irrigation has declined in high-risk states. In states like Bihar and Assam, the share of flood-related spending in total expenditure has dropped significantly since FY09. Floods continue to account for the highest share of natural disasters in the country.

articles.headline: Government to buy back 30,000 crore rupees of G-secs
articles.summary: The Centre has announced a buyback of four government securities with an aggregate face value of 30,000 crore rupees. The auction, scheduled for Thursday, include securities maturing in 2026 and 2027. The government will decide the specific buyback quantum for each individual security based on market responses.

articles.headline: NBFC body urges RBI to ease curbs on revolving credit
articles.summary: The Finance Industry Development Council (FIDC) has asked the RBI to reconsider restrictions on revolving credit products. FIDC argues that banning the restoration of repaid principal amounts would increase interest costs for MSMEs and individuals. The body suggested safeguards to address RBI concerns about loan evergreening instead of a blanket ban.

articles.headline: Bank deposits and credit contract as bulk funds are retired
articles.summary: Aggregate bank deposits declined by 6,534 crore rupees, and credit fell by 70,639 crore in the fortnight ended August 15. Analysts attribute the deposit contraction to banks retiring high-cost bulk deposits following significant inflows from the RBI's concessional swap facility. The credit-deposit ratio moderated slightly to 81.72%.

articles.headline: Government simplifies defense export rules to widen global access
articles.summary: The Ministry of Defence has merged existing open general export licence (OGEL) frameworks and increased validity from two to three years. The reform removes stakeholder consultation for non-lethal exports to most countries and international tenders. The changes aim to help defense manufacturers, especially MSMEs, access overseas markets faster.

articles.headline: Rajasthan expands digital fertilizer sale system statewide
articles.summary: The Rajasthan government is phasing in its 'Framework for Fertilizer Sale' system across the state to curb black marketing and hoarding. Following successful pilot projects in Sirohi and Rajsamand, over 12,000 metric tonnes of fertilizer have reached 78,000 genuine farmers. The digital system monitors demand and distribution in real-time.

articles.headline: Faith tourism drives housing and realty boom in Uttar Pradesh
articles.summary: Investment in formal real estate in Uttar Pradesh's religious hubs rose 66% to 1,631 crore rupees in H1 2026. Cities like Ayodhya, Varanasi, and Mathura are seeing a surge in demand for quality housing. The number of housing units in these projects jumped from 2,481 to 3,867 year-on-year, driven by the rapid development of religious destinations.

articles.headline: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh says inflation expectations must remain anchored
articles.summary: Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh stated the central bank has 'work to do' if inflation remains above 2%. Expressing confidence in the economy's overall performance, he emphasized the need for a stable relationship between financial markets and the central bank. His comments at Jackson Hole are being closely watched for future interest rate signals.

articles.headline: International support grows for jailed former Pakistan PM Imran Khan
articles.summary: Shekhar Gupta notes that cricketing icons like Michael Atherton and Pat Cummins have internationalized the fate of Imran Khan.
