While the Pakistani establishment seeks to finish his political career, his enduring popularity and global status are creating pressure. The situation reflects a winner-takes-all political system where jail or exile are the primary choices.

articles.headline: Comparison of Modinomics and Manmohanomics reveals political and economic frictions
articles.summary: R Jagannathan critiques P Chidambaram's assessment of the current economy, noting that political outcomes often trump pure economic theory. While the Modi government faces criticism for centralization and oligopolies, it has maintained a stronger macroeconomy and controlled inflation better than the UPA era. The article argues that domestic giants are necessary to compete with global firms.

articles.headline: Nifty IT index surges 3.5 percent on robust Nvidia results
articles.summary: Shares of top Indian IT firms rallied as Nvidia’s strong quarterly earnings confirmed continued global spending on AI infrastructure. Companies like Coforge, TCS, and Infosys saw significant gains, with the Nifty IT index closing at 31,281.70. Analysts believe the results ease fears of a fading AI boom and suggest a potential catch-up trade for the Indian tech sector.

articles.headline: Bernstein retains Nifty target at 26,000 despite market strength
articles.summary: Brokerage Bernstein has maintained its Nifty target at 26,000, suggesting that current earnings are driven by policy-driven 'distortions' like subsidies and GST cuts. The report highlighted that while revenue growth for top firms is strong at 12%, profit growth lags at 8%. These temporary factors may be impacting broader macro indicators and corporate earnings.

articles.headline: FPIs record highest single-day equity selling since June
articles.summary: Foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) sold 5,040 crore rupees worth of Indian equities on Friday, the highest daily selloff in over two months. The selling, largely driven by stake sales in Ather Energy and Lenskart by Singapore and Alpha Wave, was absorbed by domestic institutional investors (DIIs) who purchased 5,184 crore worth of shares.

articles.headline: Sebi clears Jio Platforms IPO and six other public offers
articles.summary: The market regulator has given the green signal for Jio Platforms’ initial public offering, comprising a fresh issue of up to 270 million shares. Sebi also cleared IPOs for Paras Healthcare, Pushp Brand India, and four others. Jio Platforms is expected to be one of the largest public issues this year, with Kotak Mahindra Capital as the lead manager.

articles.headline: Mainboard IPO listing gains hit calendar year high in August
articles.summary: August has seen the strongest listing gains for mainboard IPOs in 2026, with six of the top 10 debutants coming from this month. Tempsens Instruments India led with a 95.55% listing-day gain. Primary market sentiment remains strong ahead of mega offerings from Jio Platforms and the National Stock Exchange.

articles.headline: Sebi considers larger institutional quota for small company IPOs
articles.summary: Sebi is exploring a new quota for institutional investors in SME IPOs, similar to the rules for large companies. Up to 50% of small company share issues could be reserved for qualified institutional buyers to improve vetting. The regulator also mulls raising the size limit for firms listing on dedicated SME platforms and increasing operating profit requirements.

articles.headline: Sebi bars Debock Industries and promoter for seven years
articles.summary: Sebi has barred Debock Industries and its MD Mukesh Manveer Singh from the securities market for orchestrating a large-scale accounting fraud. Singh and associates must disgorge 59.30 crore in unlawful gains with interest. The regulator also ordered the return of 49 crore diverted from a rights issue and levied penalties exceeding 28 crore rupees.

articles.headline: Balkrishna Industries poised to outperform peers after strong Q1
articles.summary: Tyremaker Balkrishna Industries (BIL) saw its stock rise 15% in a month after reporting 24% year-on-year revenue growth in Q1. Gains were driven by higher-than-expected European volumes and improved realizations. Brokerages have raised target prices for the off-highway tyre maker, citing its deep penetration in global markets and positive outlook for CY26.

articles.headline: Investors advised to stay cautious amid gold price surge
articles.summary: Gold has gained 9.6% over the past month, driven by central bank buying and geopolitical tensions. While the bull run may continue with potential US interest rate cuts, experts recommend limiting gold allocation to 10-15% of a portfolio. Investors are advised to use systematic investment plans to average purchase prices and view gold primarily as a hedge.

articles.headline: Legal heirs liable for deceased taxpayer's dues within estate limits
articles.summary: Legal heirs may be asked to settle the tax obligations of a deceased person, but their liability is generally limited to the value of the inherited estate. Heirs must register as the taxpayer's representative on the e-filing portal to respond to notices. Distributing assets before clearing tax dues can lead to personal exposure for the legal representative.

articles.headline: India eyes Moon base and participation in Nasa lunar program
articles.summary: Nasa has invited Isro to join its Moon Base program, a significant step following India's successful soft landing near the lunar south pole. India aims to establish its own Bharatiya Antariksh Station by 2035 and send an astronaut to the Moon by 2040. The lunar race is shifting toward building permanent infrastructure for power, communications, and resource depot.

articles.headline: New book explores Mumbai's history through its diverse culinary evolution
articles.summary: Meher Mirza's 'Sea, Salt and Spice' traces Mumbai's history from the Satavahana period to the colonial era through food. The book highlights the relationship between the British and the Koli fishing community and provides insights into the origin of local names like Borivali and Chinchpokli. It examines how culinary habits were shaped by political and social structures.

articles.headline: India must view R&D as organizational learning to catch China
articles.summary: Arun Maira argues that Indian policymakers should stop viewing R&D purely as an expenditure and instead as a strategic process of building organizational capability. Comparing India to China, he notes that China's machinery production is now eight times larger than India's. He cites Telco's history as a 'learning factory' as a model for achieving international competitiveness.

articles.headline: New flood threat looms over Nepal after Himalayan glacier collapse
articles.summary: A newly formed lake at the source of a recent ice-rock avalanche poses a major flood threat to downstream regions in Nepal and China's Tibet. Space-data firm Suhora identified the 20.25-hectare lake using satellite imagery. The initial flood killed at least 547 people and left 1,500 missing. Authorities are monitoring upstream lakes as one began overflowing on Friday.

articles.headline: ITC Infotech to Acquire 44% Stake in Happiest Minds Technologies
articles.summary: ITC Infotech has set out to acquire a controlling stake in Happiest Minds Technologies from its founder and promoter Ashok Soota for approximately ₹2,900 crore. The deal will trigger a mandatory open offer for an additional 26% from public shareholders. The acquisition is expected to boost ITC Infotech's specialized digital technology services and market presence.

articles.headline: India to Pitch CBDCs for Cross-Border Payments at BRICS Summit
articles.summary: India is set to propose seamless cross-border digital payments using Central Bank Digital Currencies (CBDCs) among BRICS member states at the upcoming summit in New Delhi. The move aims to reduce transaction costs and friction within the group, potentially facilitating trade in national currencies. A high-level meeting next week will further discuss these mechanisms.

articles.headline: Government Working on FDI Clarifications for Land Border Countries
articles.summary: The Indian government is preparing clarifications on its foreign direct investment (FDI) policy to assist investors from countries sharing land borders with India, such as China. The aim is to provide greater clarity on rules governing investments, particularly addressing issues related to Press Note 3, which mandates prior government approval for such investments.

articles.headline: India Offers Rescue Teams and Aid to Flood-Hit Nepal
articles.summary: India has offered to deploy National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) teams to Nepal to assist in search-and-rescue operations following devastating flash floods. At least 320 Indians remain missing or stranded. The aid package includes medical assistance, emergency supplies, and portable bridges to restore damaged infrastructure in the flood-affected regions.

articles.headline: NRAI President Urges Focus on Hygiene Standards Over Blame Games
articles.summary: National Restaurant Association of India (NRAI) president Sagar Daryani has called for the restaurant industry to focus on improving hygiene standards instead of engaging in blame games. This follows recent controversies over hygiene lapses in prominent restaurant chains. Daryani emphasized the need for a collaborative regulatory environment to ensure food safety and consumer trust.

articles.headline: Bank Credit and Deposits Contract in First Half of August
articles.summary: The banking sector saw a contraction in both credit and deposits during the fortnight ending August 15. RBI data showed a net ₹6,534 crore of deposits were withdrawn from the system, while outstanding credit also declined. This trend suggests a potential moderation in economic activity or seasonal fluctuations in banking liquidity following a period of strong growth.

articles.headline: Government May Hold Special Parliament Session for Women's Reservation Bill
articles.summary: The Central government is considering a short special session of Parliament in late September to pass the long-pending women's reservation bill. The bill seeks to reserve one-third of seats in the Lok Sabha and state assemblies for women. The decision on timing depends on the progress of delimitation-linked legislation and achieving a two-thirds majority in both houses.

articles.headline: Mirwaiz Umar Farooq Calls for Protection of Himalayan Ecosystem
articles.summary: Islamic cleric Mirwaiz Umar Farooq has expressed concern over the fragile ecosystem of Jammu and Kashmir following devastating floods in Nepal. He emphasized that the Himalayan region is prone to climate-change-induced disasters like cloudbursts and flash floods. He called for a re-evaluation of current development patterns to mitigate environmental risks in the mountain belt.

articles.headline: BJP Accuses Congress of Using Tribal Students for Political Gain
articles.summary: The BJP in Maharashtra has accused the Congress of inciting tribal students to continue their protests in Mumbai as a means to relaunch Rahul Gandhi's political career. While the state government claims to have accepted most student demands, Congress leaders maintain that the strike will continue. Rahul Gandhi is expected to visit the protest site during his upcoming trip.

articles.headline: BJP Chief to Meet Young Leaders to Strengthen Youth Outreach
articles.summary: BJP President Nabin has called a meeting of 45 young leaders, termed the 'Special-45', to brainstorm strategies for connecting better with youth ahead of state assembly elections. The group includes Union ministers, MPs, and party leaders. The initiative aims to inject fresh ideas into the party and address the concerns of younger voters in key states like Punjab and Uttar Pradesh.

articles.headline: DMK Increases Party District Units to 110 Ahead of Elections
articles.summary: DMK president M K Stalin has announced a major administrative restructuring of the party, increasing the number of organizational districts from 77 to 110. The move aims to decentralize control, induct young blood, and strengthen the party's election machinery ahead of the 2026 Assembly elections. The restructuring also involves fixed age caps and limited terms for party posts.

articles.headline: Diaspora-Led Platforms Assist RSS in Expanding Global Outreach
articles.summary: The Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) is leveraging independent platforms led by Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) to expand its global engagement. Organizations like Hindu Forum for Engagement and Dialogue (AHEAD) are facilitating meetings between RSS leaders and international stakeholders. This strategy aims to present the Sangh's worldview on global challenges and counter criticism.

articles.headline: Gujarat Launches India's First Sports Genomics Programme
articles.summary: Gujarat has launched a first-of-its-kind sports genomics programme to understand the genetic, physiological, and performance characteristics of its athletes. The initiative aims to use scientific data to improve training, nutrition, and injury prevention. This move is part of the state's preparations for the 2030 Commonwealth Games and to build a pipeline of elite athletes.

articles.headline: Karnataka Missing from Centre's Rail Quadrupling Project Plans
articles.summary: Karnataka Infrastructure Development Minister MB Patil stated that no railway routes in the state are included in the Centre’s plan to quadruple high-density rail routes. He criticized the decision as an injustice to Karnataka, which is willing to share 50% of the project costs. The state has sought better rail connectivity to its coastal ports and high-speed city corridors.

articles.headline: India and US Sign Deal for Javelin Anti-Tank Missiles
articles.summary: The Indian Army is set to acquire Javelin anti-tank guided missiles from the US under a government-to-government initiative. A Letter of Offer and Acceptance for the $45.7 million deal was signed through the US Foreign Military Sales process. The move reflects a deepening defense partnership between the two nations and aims to bolster the Army's anti-armor capabilities on a fast track.

articles.headline: 57-Day Amarnath Yatra Concludes on Raksha Bandhan
articles.summary: The 57-day annual Amarnath Yatra concluded on Friday with the arrival of the 'Chhari Mubarak' at the holy cave shrine in south Kashmir. Over 5 lakh pilgrims visited the shrine this year. Special prayers were held to mark the end of the pilgrimage, which was conducted under tight security and faced some disruptions due to adverse weather conditions earlier in the season.

articles.headline: BRICS Nations to Adopt Framework for Resilient Supply Chains
articles.summary: BRICS nations are poised to adopt a voluntary framework for cross-border logistics and supply chain cooperation at the upcoming summit. The initiative aims to enhance the resilience and efficiency of trade within the bloc. It includes measures for knowledge sharing on cargo handling, digital infrastructure for logistics, and promoting trade in national currencies to reduce costs.

articles.headline: Opposition Slams Maharashtra Government Over Marathi Language Rule for Drivers
articles.summary: The MNS and Shiv Sena (UBT) have criticized Maharashtra Deputy CM Devendra Fadnavis for granting a one-year extension to migrant taxi and auto drivers to learn Marathi. The opposition parties allege that the decision is politically motivated ahead of upcoming elections and compromises the state's linguistic identity. They demand strict implementation of the language requirement.

articles.headline: India's Industrial Output Growth Reaches 6.7% in July
articles.summary: India's industrial output (IIP) grew by 6.7% in July, driven by a strong 10.3% expansion in the electricity sector and a 7.3% rise in manufacturing. While growth improved from the previous month, consumer durables showed an eight-month high growth of 10.5%. Economists expect growth to remain steady, though challenges from global headwinds and weak monsoon impact persist.

articles.headline: Pharmaceutical Companies May Bear Full Liability for Overcharging Risks
articles.summary: The National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA) has proposed holding drug manufacturers solely responsible for overpricing of essential medicines, potentially exempting retailers from prosecution. The move is contested by the industry, which argues that retailers should share responsibility. If implemented, manufacturers could face stiff penalties and recovery of overcharged amounts.

articles.headline: India and Canada Explore Deeper Economic Cooperation and UPI Integration
articles.summary: India and Canada have expressed interest in strengthening bilateral economic ties, with a focus on cross-border remittances and integrating UPI services. Following discussions between finance ministers, both nations are looking to resume talks on a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement. The move aims to facilitate easier financial transactions for the large Indian diaspora.

articles.headline: Global Arabica Coffee Stocks Decline to 26-Year Low
articles.summary: Arabica coffee stocks on the ICE exchange have fallen to their lowest level since May 2000, as dealers scramble for supplies amid concerns over physical market tightness. Prices have surged above $3 per lb over the past couple of months. Low inventories and strong demand from emerging markets are expected to keep prices elevated in the global market in the near term.

articles.headline: Government Implements Fortnightly Sugar Quotas to Stabilize Domestic Prices
articles.summary: To curb rising sugar prices and ensure domestic availability, the Indian government has introduced a fortnightly quota system for mill-wise sales starting in September. Mills will be required to sell 20% of their monthly quota in the first week and the remainder subsequently. The move aims to prevent hoarding and stabilize prices ahead of the upcoming festive season.

articles.headline: Renewable Energy Firms Can Now Sell Curtailed Power on Exchanges
articles.summary: The Ministry of Power has allowed renewable energy (RE) generators to sell electricity that is curtailed under general network access on power exchanges. This move aims to prevent wastage of green energy and provide additional revenue streams for generators. To facilitate this, generators can use energy storage systems or sell the surplus power through other market segments.

articles.headline: India to Promote Ethical AI Framework at SCO Summit
articles.summary: India is set to pitch a global agenda for inclusive and ethical artificial intelligence at the upcoming Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) summit in Kyrgyzstan. New Delhi aims to highlight its seven chakras of AI governance, focusing on human-centric systems and safety. The move is seen as an effort to counter China's influence in setting multilateral AI standards.

articles.headline: TCS Reduces Variable Pay for Senior Employees Amid Profit Pressures
articles.summary: Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) has reduced the variable pay for its mid-to-senior level employees to 50-70% for the first quarter of the fiscal year. The cut comes as the IT major faces margin pressure and a slowdown in demand. While junior employees continue to receive full variable pay, senior staff are seeing reductions reflecting the company's cautious financial outlook.

articles.headline: Tencent Releases Open-Source AI Model Specialized for Coding
articles.summary: Chinese tech giant Tencent has released an open-source AI model, Hy4-preview, specifically designed for software engineering and coding tasks. The model, available on Hugging Face, uses a mixture-of-experts architecture with 770 billion parameters. It aims to compete with other leading coding assistants by offering high performance in complex programming and debugging queries.

articles.headline: Icertis Replaced CEO Following Internal Whistleblower Allegations
articles.summary: Enterprise tech firm Icertis reportedly replaced its CEO following a whistleblower letter alleging a lack of transparency and poor culture within the organization. The company has appointed interim co-CEOs while it searches for a permanent successor. Icertis stated that the leadership change was part of a planned transition, but sources indicate the internal complaint triggered it.

articles.headline: India Aligns Mobile Tower Radiation Norms with Global Standards
articles.summary: India has eased its mobile tower radiation (EMF) limits, aligning them with global standards set by the ICNIRP. The permitted power density for 5G base stations has been increased tenfold. This move is expected to improve 5G service quality, reduce the number of towers needed, and lower network rollout costs for telecom operators, potentially leading to better coverage.

articles.headline: Unsealed Documents Reveal Rupert Murdoch's Plan to Reunite Media Empire
articles.summary: Recently unsealed court documents have revealed Rupert Murdoch's plan to re-merge his media companies, News Corp and Fox Corp, into a single entity. The move, which was reportedly met with resistance from some family members and shareholders, aimed to consolidate control and create a more efficient media conglomerate. The plans have since been officially abandoned.

articles.headline: HAL Reports Record Turnover and Profits in Annual General Meeting
articles.summary: Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL) announced a record turnover of ₹31,792 crore for the fiscal year 2025-26, a 6% growth from the previous year. The company's profit after tax increased by 9% to ₹9,076 crore. HAL highlighted its achievements in indigenous defense production, including the delivery of LCA Mk1A aircraft and its contributions to India's recent space missions.

articles.headline: Indian Stocks Rally as Sensex Gains 331 Points on FPI Buying
articles.summary: Indian equity markets ended Friday on a positive note, with the BSE Sensex gaining 331 points to close at 77,265. The rally was driven by strong foreign portfolio investor (FPI) buying and positive global cues. Mid-cap and small-cap stocks also saw gains, reflecting overall market optimism despite ongoing concerns over high valuations in some specific market segments.

articles.headline: Nearly Half of BSE 200 Stocks Give No Returns This Year
articles.summary: Analysis shows that nearly 50% of stocks in the BSE 200 index have yielded zero or negative returns so far in 2026, despite the benchmark hitting record highs. The divergence highlights stress in sectors like FMCG, IT, and cement. This trend indicates that the market rally is narrowly driven by a few large-cap stocks, while the broader market faces significant selling pressure.

articles.headline: India's Forex Reserves Reach Record High of $729.3 Billion
articles.summary: India's foreign exchange reserves surged by $2.8 billion to reach a record high of $729.3 billion for the week ending August 21. The increase was fueled by the RBI's mopping up of dollar inflows from non-resident deposits. The record reserves provide a significant cushion against global economic shocks and support the long-term stability of the Indian rupee in the market.

articles.headline: Tempsens Instruments Debuts with Over 100% Gains on Stock Exchange
articles.summary: Shares of temperature sensing solutions provider Tempsens Instruments made a stellar debut on the stock exchange, listing at more than double its IPO price. The stock surged to ₹631.20 against an issue price of ₹300, marking a 110% gain. It is the biggest listing-day gainer this year, reflecting strong investor appetite for high-growth industrial and tech sector firms.

articles.headline: Court Rejects Zee Group Founder's Settlement Offer Over Debt Issues
articles.summary: A Mumbai court has rejected a proposed settlement from Zee Group founder Subhash Chandra regarding ₹22,000 crore in personal guarantees. Creditors had raised concerns about the transparency of the offer and the involvement of related parties. The court emphasized the need for a thorough forensic audit to verify asset valuations and ensure fair recovery for the involved lenders.

articles.headline: Vodka Gains Market Share in India's Spirits Market
articles.summary: Vodka's share in India's spirits market has risen to 6.1%, up from 3.8% in 2025, as younger consumers increasingly prefer white spirits over traditional brown spirits. The shift is driven by new product launches, innovative flavors, and a growing cocktail culture. Major players like Radico Khaitan are seeing a significant boost in sales as they expand their premium vodka portfolios.

articles.headline: US Pause on Green Card Interviews Impacts Thousands of Indian Applicants
articles.summary: The US government's decision to pause in-person interviews for certain green card categories has left thousands of Indian professionals in a state of uncertainty. The move, attributed to administrative backlog and policy shifts, affects those applying for employment-based and family-sponsored visas. Legal experts advise applicants to monitor status updates closely for any changes.

articles.headline: Oil India and IOC Relinquish Gabon Oil Block After Extension Denied
articles.summary: Oil India and Indian Oil Corporation have relinquished an exploration block in Gabon after the local government rejected their request for a license extension. The consortium had invested over $10 million in the block but faced delays due to the pandemic and technical challenges. The move highlights the risks faced by Indian state-run firms in international oil exploration ventures.

articles.headline: Coal India Concerned Over Reduced Incentives for Coal Gasification Projects
articles.summary: Coal India has expressed concern that the government's decision to reduce the bidding window for coal gasification projects might blunt the effectiveness of its incentive scheme. The company argues that a shorter window makes it difficult for potential investors to prepare detailed project reports. The ₹37,500 crore incentive scheme aims to promote cleaner use of coal.

articles.headline: PCB Almost Pulled Out of England Test Over Imran Khan Interview
articles.summary: The Pakistan Cricket Board reportedly considered withdrawing its players from the second Test against England after an interview with jailed former PM Imran Khan was aired during lunch. The PCB objected to the broadcast, citing political sensitivities. The situation was resolved after discussions between board officials and broadcasters, and the match proceeded as scheduled.

articles.headline: Italy's Serie A Emerges as Top Spender in European Football Market
articles.summary: Italy's Serie A has emerged as a top spender in the current European football transfer market, with clubs investing over €1 billion on new players. While England's Premier League remains the wealthiest, Serie A's spending reflects a renewed financial confidence among its top teams. Major signings by clubs like Juventus and AC Milan have driven the league's high expenditure this season.

articles.headline: Indian Women's Hockey Team Captain Optimistic About Future Growth
articles.summary: Indian women's hockey team captain Savita Punia has expressed optimism about the team's future despite a recent string of losses. She highlighted the team's progress in international rankings and the emergence of talented young players. Savita emphasized the need for consistent exposure and better infrastructure to help the team compete at the highest level globally.

articles.headline: Over 1,000 Additional Athletes Included for Upcoming Asian Games
articles.summary: Organizers of the upcoming Asian Games have added over 1,000 participants to the final list of athletes following requests from member nations. The games, to be held in Nagoya, Japan, will now feature approximately 15,000 athletes competing across various disciplines. The addition aims to provide more opportunities for athletes to showcase their talent on a continental stage.

articles.headline: History of Food Rules and Their Impact on Global Trade
articles.summary: An analysis of how religious dietary laws, such as Kosher and Halal, historically acted as passports for global trade. These rules helped build networks of trust among traders across different regions and religions. By adhering to shared dietary standards, merchants could establish reliable business partnerships and credit systems, facilitating the flow of goods over long distances.

articles.headline: Nepal Floods Serve as Warning to Respect Himalayan River Systems
articles.summary: The recent catastrophic floods in Nepal highlight the devastating impact of disregarding natural river systems in the fragile Himalayan region. Rapid urbanization and poorly planned infrastructure projects have worsened the effects of climate-change-induced disasters. The article calls for a more sustainable approach to development that respects environmental limits.

articles.headline: Red hexagonal warning labels for high-fat junk foods receive Supreme Court nod
articles.summary: The Supreme Court has approved the implementation of FSSAI's plan to place red hexagonal warning labels on packaged foods high in fat, sugar, or salt. The court noted that these clear visual warnings are essential for public health, especially for children. The labels must be prominently displayed to inform consumers of the health risks associated with the product's nutritional content.

articles.headline: Karnataka Minister B Nagendra Resigns Over Valmiki Corporation Scam
articles.summary: Karnataka Planning and Statistics Minister B Nagendra resigned from the Cabinet following intense pressure from the BJP opposition over the alleged Maharshi Valmiki Scheduled Tribes Development Corporation scam. Nagendra stated he was stepping down to prevent embarrassment to the Congress leadership while maintaining his innocence regarding the alleged financial irregularities.

articles.headline: Sonia Gandhi Book Deal Fails Over Refusal to Delete Portions
articles.summary: Congress leader Sonia Gandhi’s book deal with Penguin Random House India fell through after she refused to delete references to PM Narendra Modi, the RSS, and Chinese intrusions. Gandhi maintained her memoir, 'Belonging: A Journey of Love,' must remain an undistorted account of her life. HarperCollins is reportedly finalizing an agreement to publish the Indian edition of the book.

articles.headline: India and United States sign deal for Javelin anti-tank missiles
articles.summary: India has signed an agreement with the US to procure Javelin anti-tank guided missiles for the Indian Army. The deal includes a letter of offer and acceptance (LOA) for the shoulder-fired man-portable systems, which are effective against armored vehicles. The agreement also includes provisions for future technical cooperation and potential local co-production of the defense systems.

articles.headline: Praggnanandhaa Becomes First Indian to Win Grand Chess Tour Title
articles.summary: Grandmaster R Praggnanandhaa has made history by becoming the first Indian to win the prestigious Grand Chess Tour title. He secured the victory after a stunning performance in the final round of the Saint Louis Rapid & Blitz tournament. The win cements his position as one of the world's top chess players and a rising star in the international chess circuit.

articles.headline: Infosys executive Gopisetty reported unreachable following devastating Nepal floods
articles.summary: Lax Gopisetty, the CEO of Infosys Public Services, is reported to be unreachable after the massive flash floods in Nepal. The company confirmed that he was visiting the region in a personal capacity when the disaster struck. Infosys stated they are in close communication with his family and relevant authorities to track his status and ensure his well-being.

articles.headline: TMC National General Secretary Abhishek Banerjee Booked Over Office Scuffle
articles.summary: Kolkata police have filed FIRs against TMC leaders Abhishek Banerjee and Derek O’Brien following a scuffle at Banerjee's office. The incident occurred when municipal officials tried to remove an allegedly illegal billboard. Thirteen people were arrested on charges of attacking police. A Kolkata court has remanded the arrested individuals to police custody until September 3.

articles.headline: Nilekani Task Force Invites Public Suggestions for Exam System Reform
articles.summary: A high-powered task force led by Nandan Nilekani has invited suggestions from stakeholders to reform India’s public examination system. The panel is focusing on improving exam integrity, transparency, and student well-being through better use of technology. Feedback on computer-based testing and governance can be submitted via the task force website until September 13.

articles.headline: Finance Ministry Drafts New Framework to Boost Infrastructure Funding
articles.summary: The finance ministry is preparing a financing framework to widen the funding pool for infrastructure beyond traditional banks. With an investment requirement of ₹150 trillion till FY31, the plan aims to strengthen underwriting and deepen debt markets. A proposed centre of excellence will standardize project reports to accelerate financial closure for long-gestation projects.

articles.headline: India and Canada Initiate Bilateral Investment Treaty Negotiations
articles.summary: India and Canada expressed readiness to begin negotiations for a bilateral investment treaty following an Economic and Financial Dialogue in Toronto. Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman highlighted the need for closer cooperation amid global economic uncertainty. The two nations aim to expand trade to CAD 70 billion by 2030 through a comprehensive economic partnership agreement.

articles.headline: Reliance Jio Receives SEBI Approval for India's Largest IPO
articles.summary: Reliance Jio Infocomm has received approval from the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) for its initial public offering (IPO), which is expected to be the largest in India's history. The company aims to raise between $3.5 billion and $4 billion, valuing the telecom major at approximately $100 billion. The proceeds will be used to pay off debt and expand infrastructure.

articles.headline: Bajaj Auto Subsidiary KTM Reports First Profit Since Insolvency
articles.summary: Austrian bike maker KTM, majority-owned by Bajaj Auto, reported its first operating profit since restructuring. The company achieved an Ebit of €1.3 million in the April-June quarter, supported by workforce cuts and reduced inventory. Revenue jumped 61% to €370 million, signaling a successful turnaround for the premium motorcycle brand following its bankruptcy filing.

articles.headline: Neeraj Chopra Qualifies for Diamond League Finals With Season Best
articles.summary: Indian javelin thrower Neeraj Chopra qualified for the Diamond League Finals in Brussels after a season-best throw of 88.05 meters in Lausanne. Despite competing in only two one-day meetings, his performance earned him 12 points and a spot in the elite final. Chopra finished second in the Lausanne event, further cementing his status as a top global competitor.

articles.headline: Noel Tata and Shapoorji Pallonji Group discuss share swap for stake sale
articles.summary: The Tata Group is in talks with the Shapoorji Pallonji (SP) Group regarding a potential share swap to unlock liquidity and settle long-standing disputes. The proposal involves the SP Group surrendering part or all of its 18.4% stake in Tata Sons in exchange for shares in listed Tata companies like Tata Power. The move could help the SP Group repay its substantial debt.

articles.headline: TVS Motor Appoints Peyman Kargar as Its Next Chief Executive
articles.summary: TVS Motor Company has named Peyman Kargar, its current head of international business, as its next chief executive officer. Kargar will take over the role in January 2027, succeeding the current CEO. The appointment aims to bolster TVS's global expansion strategy, particularly in key markets like Africa, Asia, and the Middle East, where it already has a growing presence.

articles.headline: Bharti Airtel Leads Telecom Subscriber Additions in July
articles.summary: Bharti Airtel added 26.8 lakh mobile subscribers in July, outpacing Reliance Jio, which added 24.4 lakh users. According to TRAI data, Vodafone Idea continued to lose subscribers, while state-run BSNL saw a marginal increase. The total number of mobile connections in India grew slightly, reflecting steady demand for telecom services despite recent tariff hikes by major operators.

articles.headline: IndiGo's Venture Capital Arm Invests in AI Startup Sarvam AI
articles.summary: Indigo Ventures, the venture capital arm of IndiGo airline, has invested an undisclosed amount in artificial intelligence startup Sarvam AI. The investment aims to explore AI applications in the aviation industry, such as improving customer experience and optimizing operational efficiency. This marks the fund's first investment in the AI space since its recent launch.

articles.headline: Sammaan Capital Will Not Challenge Subhash Chandra Repayment Plan
articles.summary: Sammaan Capital, formerly Indiabulls Housing Finance, has stated it will not challenge the NCLT approval of Zee founder Subhash Chandra’s repayment plan. The lender noted it has already collected an amount exceeding the original disbursement through previous enforcement and recovery measures under the Sarfaesi Act.

articles.headline: Over 320 Indians missing in Nepal following flash floods
articles.summary: At least 320 Indian nationals are contactable or missing in Nepal after Wednesday's flash floods. The Ministry of External Affairs has set up control rooms and confirmed that 400 people stranded in the Tibet Autonomous Region are safe. India is sending planeloads of relief material to help with the rescue and recovery efforts as the death toll continues to rise.

articles.headline: Road ministry mandates progressive reduction of pedal assistance for e-cycles
articles.summary: New draft norms from the Road Transport Ministry mandate a progressive reduction in motor power assistance for electric cycles as they approach their maximum speed of 25 kmph. This technical requirement is intended to ensure these vehicles remain in the low-speed category and are not used as unregistered high-speed motorbikes. The move aims to improve road safety for cyclists and pedestrians.

articles.headline: Reserve Bank of India reports foreign exchange reserves hit record 729 billion
articles.summary: India’s foreign exchange reserves have reached an all-time high of $729.8 billion, driven by a surge in central bank strategy on NRI deposits. The reserves increased by $12.4 billion in a single week. This strong position provides a significant buffer against global economic volatility and helps stabilize the rupee. Most of the growth came from foreign currency assets and gold reserves.

articles.headline: Industrial output in India expands 4.7 percent in July led by manufacturing
articles.summary: India’s industrial production grew by 4.7% in July 2026, supported by steady performance in the manufacturing and power sectors. The Index of Industrial Production (IIP) showed that 19 out of 23 manufacturing sub-groups recorded positive growth. The capital goods sector also saw significant expansion, indicating improved investment sentiment and increased demand for industrial machinery.

articles.headline: Meta India VP Sandhya Devanathan Joins OpenAI as SE Asia Lead
articles.summary: Sandhya Devanathan, vice president of Meta India and Southeast Asia, is joining OpenAI to lead its operations in Southeast Asia and Australia. After a decade at Meta, she will be responsible for OpenAI's growth in consumer and enterprise spaces, partnerships, and operations starting in October. She will be based in Singapore to oversee the region's regulatory and market expansion.

articles.headline: India finishes fifth in FIH Pro League after loss to Belgium
articles.summary: The Indian women's hockey team finished their FIH Pro League campaign in fifth place after a 2-1 defeat to Belgium in their final match. Despite the loss, Hockey India announced a cash award of Rs 50 lakh for the team in recognition of their competitive performance throughout the season. The team’s coach highlighted the growth in physical and mental strength of the players during the tournament.

articles.headline: West Bengal BJP leader Suvendu Adhikari vows to clean up Jadavpur University
articles.summary: Leader of Opposition in West Bengal Suvendu Adhikari has criticized the state government for failing to curb "anti-national" activities at Jadavpur University. Following reports of "Azadi" slogans being raised during a campus protest, Adhikari vowed that the BJP would take steps to restore the institution's reputation. He called for a strict investigation into the student outfits involved in the demonstration.

articles.headline: Reliance Industries rejects allegations of market manipulation by Subhash Chandra
articles.summary: Reliance Industries Limited (RIL) has issued a statement rejecting allegations made by Essel Group chairman Subhash Chandra regarding market manipulation. Chandra had accused RIL of orchestrating a campaign against his company to prevent its merger with Sony. RIL described the claims as "baseless and malicious," stating that it has always adhered to the highest standards of corporate governance.

articles.headline: Renewables generated one-fifth of power in July
articles.summary: Renewables accounted for a record 20% of India's cumulative power generation in July, a significant increase from previous years. This feat coincided with a surge in power demand, which rose by nearly 11% year-on-year to 171 billion units, the highest on record for any month. The share of coal in the generation mix declined to a 10-month low.

articles.headline: Hero MotoCorp Increases Stake in Electric Scooter Maker Ather Energy
articles.summary: Hero MotoCorp is raising its stake in electric two-wheeler startup Ather Energy by approximately 3% through a ₹1,758 crore secondary transaction. This acquisition will increase Hero's total shareholding in Ather to 18.6%. The move underscores Hero's commitment to the growing EV market and follows Ather's plans for an IPO to expand its manufacturing and R&D capacity.

articles.headline: RBI to Buy Back ₹30,000 Crore of Government Securities
articles.summary: The Reserve Bank of India has announced plans to buy back ₹30,000 crore worth of government securities maturing in FY27. The move is intended to reduce the government's debt repayment burden and manage liquidity in the financial system. The buyback is part of the central bank's regular market operations to support fiscal stability and smooth out maturing debt obligations.

articles.headline: Alpha Wave Global sells 1.7 percent stake in Lenskart
articles.summary: Global asset firm Alpha Wave Global divested a 1.7% stake in Lenskart Solutions for approximately 1,856 crore rupees through block deals on the NSE. The shares were sold at an average price of 630 rupees each. Following the transaction, Alpha Wave's remaining stake in the Gurugram-based eyewear retailer is roughly 2.95%.

articles.headline: Govt expects 25,000 registrations under Parivartan scheme by October
articles.summary: The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways expects 25,000 registrations under the Parivartan scheme by October. Launched in July to phase out polluting commercial vehicles in Delhi-NCR, the scheme offers incentives like tax concessions and fuel vouchers. Over 2 lakh old trucks and buses in the region are eligible for replacement.

articles.headline: CII panel moots creation of GFI to mobilise funds
articles.summary: A CII panel has proposed establishing a dedicated Green Finance Institution (GFI) to mobilise significant capital for green infrastructure and transition. The GFI would focus on mid-sized companies and MSMEs, offering credit guarantees and attracting private investment. It also suggests a legally authorised mechanism for public carbon-related revenue.

articles.headline: New Appointments Made to National Testing Agency Leadership
articles.summary: The Centre has appointed two directors and a joint director to the National Testing Agency (NTA). Ravi Kumar Singh and Prasanna Venkatesh V have been appointed as directors, while Amit Samdariya has been selected as joint director. These appointments come amid scrutiny of the NTA regarding exam irregularities and aim to strengthen its administrative and operational framework.

articles.headline: Nepal floods: 21 Indians arrive but 320 still remain ‘uncontactable’
articles.summary: At least 320 Indians remain missing and around 400 others are stranded in Nepal following devastating flash floods. India has dispatched humanitarian aid and rescue teams, with 21 Indians arriving safely in New Delhi. Parts of Bihar also face flood threats due to swollen rivers and swollen river levels.

articles.headline: BioNTech to terminate mRNA cancer vaccine trial
articles.summary: BioNTech SE has decided to terminate the mid-stage trial of its experimental mRNA cancer vaccine. The vaccine was being evaluated as an adjuvant monotherapy in high-risk colorectal cancer patients. This decision follows the vaccine's evaluation for specific patient groups.

articles.headline: China Attributes Flash Floods in Nepal to Glacier Collapse
articles.summary: Beijing has stated that the collapse of a high-altitude glacier in Nepal triggered the massive flash flood disaster. Scientists are investigating how a glacial collapse and ice-rock avalanche may have released dammed waters. Assessments indicate that debris temporarily blocked the Lhende River, creating a landslide dam that subsequently gave way, causing the floods.

articles.headline: Rising exports lift IndiGo announces investment in Sarvam, steps up AI focus
articles.summary: IndiGo has announced an investment in Sarvam AI, signalling a focus on AI-led technologies for customer experience and operations. This partnership aims to leverage AI for improved customer engagement and innovation. IndiGo sees AI as foundational for the aviation industry's future.

articles.headline: Amid AI automation, firms look for polymath engineers
articles.summary: Companies are increasingly seeking 'polymath' engineers who possess cross-domain skills, blending technical depth with business acumen. AI automation is driving demand for hybrid roles like FDEs and GTM engineers. This shift reflects a need for talent that can bridge technology, business, and multiple disciplines.

articles.headline: Tata Sons Granted Three-Month Extension for Annual General Meeting
articles.summary: The Registrar of Companies has granted Tata Sons a three-month extension to hold its annual general meeting, originally due by September 30. This is the first time the group's holding company has sought such an extension. The delay is reportedly due to a lack of quorum following a decision by the charity commissioner regarding the participation of certain trustees in the meeting.

articles.headline: Indian Cities Lead APAC Region in Logistics Rental Growth
articles.summary: Mumbai and Bengaluru have recorded the highest rental growth for logistics space in the Asia-Pacific region, according to a report by Knight Frank. Demand is driven by e-commerce, third-party logistics, and a push for modern warehouse facilities. Rentals in Mumbai rose by 5.3% year-on-year, reflecting the robust growth of India's manufacturing and retail sectors.

articles.headline: Quick Commerce Platforms See Surge in Last-Minute Rakhi Sales
articles.summary: Quick-commerce platforms like Blinkit, Zepto, and Swiggy Instamart saw a significant surge in orders for Raksha Bandhan. Last-minute gifting, including rakhi sets, dry fruits, and premium chocolates, drove high sales volumes. Some platforms reported nearly 300% year-on-year growth in orders as consumers increasingly opt for rapid delivery services for festive essentials.

articles.headline: India's First Dedicated Quantum and AI University to Open in Amaravati
articles.summary: Andhra Pradesh is set to establish India's first dedicated university for quantum computing and artificial intelligence in Amaravati. The 8.5-acre campus will be funded through a grant from the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology. The university aims to train 8,250 learners over five years in advanced fields like machine learning and semiconductor fabrication.
